articles.title: Asian stocks slump after US tech rout amid AI jitters
articles.summary: Concerns that Democrats in the US will push back against data center projects are weighing on an AI trade that is already on shaky footing amid growing doubts about profitability.

image.caption: US markets were hammered on Thursday by a sharp retreat in tech stocksImage: Brendan McDermid/REUTERS

blocks.text: Japanese and South Korean shares tumbled on Friday, following a massive selloff in tech stocks on Wall Street the previous day.

Tokyo's benchmark Nikkei 225 index fell 5.5% in early trade, while Seoul's tech-heavy Kospi index slid as much as 8.8%, triggering a circuit breaker which suspended trading for 20 minutes. Taiwan's benchmark TAIEX index was also down more than 8%.
Asian tech giants including Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) have borne the brunt of the artificial intelligence-related selloff.
Samsung plunged nearly 10% while SK Hynix slid over 11%.
Chip-related shares in Japan also took a beating, with Tokyo Electron stock trading down around 9% and Kioxia shedding 13%.
European stock futures fell 1%, indicating that the selloff was likely to spread across to Europe.
Data centers face backlash from US communities
What's behind the stock rout on Wall Street?
On Thursday, US markets were hammered by a sharp retreat in tech stocks, particularly those involved in the buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure like data centers.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 5.52% and shed as much as $2.5 trillion (roughly €2.23 trillion) in market value, while the broader S&P 500 index plunged 4.4%.
The rout occurred as investors grow increasingly anxious about the colossal AI spending plans and whether they will eventually produce commensurate profits.
The results of the US midterm elections, which saw Democrats seize control of both houses of US Congress, added to the concerns.

A number of Democratic governors-elect campaigned on slowing artificial intelligence development and promised to stop or pause the construction of data centers amid growing public opposition to such projects.
"It's pretty clear there's been a real shift ​in sentiment," Michael McCarthy, chief executive for Australia and New Zealand at online brokerage Moomoo, told the Reuters news agency.

"Market turning points are often accompanied by strong disagreement, and that shows up in the market ​by huge swings in either direction," he said. "That's what we appear to have had — and last night's emphatic sell-down suggests that is the direction that we're now headed in."

articles.summary: FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman says the government is 'seeing these systems targeted across critical infrastructure sectors globally'

blocks.text: REFRIGERATORS. View of empty refrigerators at the frozen food aisle inside an Intermarche supermarket in Paris the day after a cyberattack targeted refrigeration systems at French supermarket chains, causing food losses and fires at several stores, France, October 13, 2026.
Lucien Libert/Reuters
FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman says the government is 'seeing these systems targeted across critical infrastructure sectors globally'

items: The United States government has issued a warning about an ongoing cyber threat targeting industrial refrigeration systems, urging organizations reliant on cold storage to be vigilant.
Malicious cyber actors are exploiting vulnerabilities in internet-accessible refrigeration controllers, which could lead to dangerous consequences like fire hazards and inventory loss.
Authorities recommend that operators of these systems disconnect them from the public internet, isolate them from corporate networks, and apply necessary software updates to mitigate risks.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

WASHINGTON, USA – The United States is warning of an “ongoing cyber threat” to industrial refrigeration systems, saying in a statement issued on Thursday, November 5, that every organization that depends on cold storage should assume it could fall into the hackers’ crosshairs.

The statement, which follows a spate of hacks against commercial freezers in the United States and Europe, said that unidentified “malicious cyber actors” were targeting vulnerabilities in internet-accessible electronic temperature and commercial refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage facilities.
Although short on detail about the hackers involved, the statement suggested that the threat to commercial cold storage was ongoing.

“If successfully exploited, the actors could change the temperature and possibly cause physical impacts such as fire hazards, loss of inventory and changes to the service life of the system,” said the statement, which was jointly issued by the FBI, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and the departments of health, transport and agriculture.
“Every organization that depends on refrigeration and monitoring systems should assume it could be a target,” said Chris Butera, CISA’s acting executive assistant director for cybersecurity.
FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman said that the government was “seeing these systems targeted across critical infrastructure sectors globally.”

The government urged operators of industrial refrigeration control systems to pull their devices off the public internet, isolate them from their corporate networks and promptly apply software updates.

At least three waves of hacks have hit commercial fridges and freezers in the past few months. Pentagon investigators are treating a series of mysterious malfunctions that hit grocery store refrigeration units on US military bases in August as a cyberattack, Reuters first reported last week. A sweeping hack of French freezers last month dealt tens of millions of euros’ worth of damage, while a second wave of hacking affected more than 100 stores across Europe on Monday.
The hacks have raised concerns over the ability of hackers to remotely tamper with refrigerators and other critical devices. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Sara Duterte defense team expected to present witness on November 9 --Hontiveros
articles.summary: The defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte is expected to begin presenting its witnesses and evidence when the impeachment trial resumes on November 9, Senator Risa Hontiveros said Friday.

blocks.text: IMPEACHMENT TRIAL
Published November 6, 2026 10:33am
The defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte is expected to begin presenting its witnesses and evidence when the impeachment trial resumes on November 9, Senator Risa Hontiveros said Friday.
In an interview on GMA News' Unang Balita, Hontiveros said it would be the defense panel's turn to present its case on Article II of the impeachment complaint or Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth.
"Turn na po nila ngayong trial magpresenta ng kanilang mga witnesses at ebidensya, partikular doon sa Article II," Hontiveros said.
(It is their turn now in this trial to present their witnesses and evidence, particularly in Article II.)
She said the defense panel is expected to inform the senator-judges on Monday how it intends to proceed after consulting with Duterte, the respondent in the impeachment trial.
Asked about the 20 witnesses requested by the defense, Hontiveros said she could not yet confirm whether all of them had committed to attend the proceedings.
“Malalaman natin finally kung sino-sino sa kanila at ilan lahat ang haharap sa pag-presentation na po ng defense panel sa November 9,” she said.
(We will finally know who they are and how many will appear in total when the defense panel presentson November 9.)
The impeachment trial is set to resume on Monday, November 9.

articles.title: Liberal bus crashes into shop awning on its first outing of Victorian election campaign
articles.summary:
Opposition leader Jess Wilson grimaced as the ‘Jess Express’, carrying Liberals and reporters, backs into the structure in suburban Melbourne

  • Get our

blocks.text: The Victorian Liberal party’s first offical day on the campaign trail has hit a snag, after its campaign bus reversed into the awning of a shopfront.
The “Jess Express”, a large blue bus emblazoned with an image of the opposition leader, Jess Wilson, was unveiled on Friday, 12 days after Labor launched its own red equivalent.
Featuring Wilson’s slogan, “A Fresh Start for Victoria”, the bus also carries a warning to motorists on its rear: “Dodging Labor’s potholes.”
But it wasn’t Labor’s potholes or political spin that brought the bus undone.

Arriving at Centre Road in Bentleigh for a street walk with Liberal candidate Tynan Putt, the bus was attempting to back into a parking spot when it struck the awning of a jewellery store, damaging the structure. The store was closed at the time.

blocks.caption: The Victorian Liberal campaign bus carrying leader Jess Wilson and journalists collided with a shop awning in Melbourne. Photograph: Benita Kolovos/The Guardian

blocks.text: Wilson grimaced as the incident unfolded, before quipping that the store’s owners wouldn’t have trouble finding the culprit, given her face was plastered across the side of the bus.
The Liberal campaign promptly contacted the store’s owners to provide its details, while the bus escaped with minor scratches. No one on board was injured.
Just hours earlier, its passengers – made up of party members and reporters – read safety cards offering a “guide to surviving 12 years of Labor”.

Instructions included “please remain seated and brace for potholes”, “remain calm” in the event of a “financial emergency” and a warning that passengers may experience “motion sickness” due to “Labor’s constant spin”.
“Please look towards the fresh start on the horizon,” the cards read.

It’s not the first time a campaign bus has caused a political headache. During the final week of the 2025 federal election campaign, Peter Dutton’s bus became stuck after mounting a raised concrete divider and bike lane barrier on Pitt Street in the Sydney CBD.

blocks.caption: Peter Dutton’s bus got stuck during the 2025 federal election campaign. Photograph: Mick Tsikas/AAP

blocks.text: The bus was stuck for about 40 minutes, causing traffic diversions and delaying the opposition leader’s schedule.
after newsletter promotion
At the 2023 New South Wales state election, the then opposition leader, Chris Minns opted for a zero-emissions bus that broke down after hitting a speed bump in western Sydney.
“I forgot to charge it last night and as a result it broke down,” Minns said at the time.
Journalists were promptly carted into a replacement, petrol-powered, bus.
In 2022, the Liberals in Victoria didn’t opt for a bus, instead debuting their “Ditch Danmobile” – a 1970s-style ambulance emblazoned with slogans.

Within an hour, the head of the Victorian Ambulance Union, questioned whether the stunt was legal, given state laws banning use of the word “ambulance” on any vehicle not owned or operated by an ambulance service without permission from the health department.

blocks.caption: The Liberal campaign bus was scratched when it accidentally hit an awning while reversing. Photograph: Jay Kogler/AAP

blocks.text: Current polling suggests the Coalition is well ahead of Labor, with the latest Newspoll putting it ahead 55-45 on a two-party-preferred basis.

The Liberals have Bentleigh firmly in its sights, despite Labor MP Nick Staikos holding the seat on an 8% margin. The electorate is considered a bellwether, having been won by the party forming government at 14 of the 16 elections since it was first contested in 1967.
Putt said the main issues in the electorate were cost of living and crime.
Victorians go to the polls on 28 November.

articles.title: Unemployment edges up to 5.4% in September 2026
articles.summary: Part of the increase in unemployment is due to job creation lagging behind a growing pool of workers

blocks.text: Pasay residents looking for work queue for interviews during a job fair at the Pasay City Astrodome on April 13, 2026.
Rappler
Part of the increase in unemployment is due to job creation lagging behind a growing pool of workers

items: The unemployment rate in the Philippines rose to 5.4% in September 2026, with 2.86 million Filipinos unemployed, an increase from 2.77 million in August.
The labor force grew by 1.63 million to 53.19 million, but employment only increased by 721,000, leading to a significant rise in unemployment compared to the previous year.
While some industries like accommodation and food services saw job gains, the construction sector experienced notable job losses, particularly in building and utility projects.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The Philippines’ unemployment rate slightly rose to 5.4% in September 2026 as the number of Filipinos joining the labor force continued to outpace employment growth.
Around 2.86 million Filipinos were unemployed in September, up from 2.77 million in August, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) on Friday, November 6.

The latest figure is also much higher than the 3.8% unemployment rate recorded in September 2025, when around 1.96 million Filipinos were unemployed. This meant an additional 909,000 Filipinos were without jobs compared with a year before.
Part of the increase in unemployment is due to job creation lagging behind a growing pool of workers.

National Statistician Dennis Mapa said the country’s labor force grew by around 1.63 million year-on-year to 53.19 million in September. However, employment increased by only 721,000 to 50.32 million over the same time.

Most of the increase in labor force participation came from younger Filipinos aged 15 to 24, with around 988,000 more people in this age group joining the labor force compared with September 2025. Among them, not everyone found employment, with only 606,000 securing a job.
Despite the higher unemployment rate, several industries posted substantial employment gains.

Accommodation and food service activities recorded the largest year-on-year increase, adding around 834,000 workers. Mapa said much of the increase came from restaurants, mobile food services, and canteens, as part of more economic activity ahead of the Christmas season.
Transportation and storage added another 254,000 workers, while other service activities gained 174,000.
Construction, however, continued to weaken, losing around 271,000 workers year-on-year and another 416,000 compared with August alone.

Mapa attributed the decline partly to slowing government construction projects and higher construction material costs. Employment losses were particularly pronounced in the construction of buildings, electrical installation, and construction of utility projects.
The PSA also reported a substantial drop in employment of clerical support workers, which fell by 582,000 year-on-year, the largest decline among the major occupational groups.

Asked by Rappler about the decline, Mapa said around 289,000 of the reduction came from contact center information clerks, an occupational category that includes some business process outsourcing (BPO) employees.General office clerks accounted for another 149,000 of the decline.
Underemployment, meanwhile, improved to 11% in September from 11.9% in August and 11.1% in September 2025. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Senate impeachment court applies sub judice rule to all articles of impeachment
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court has ruled that the sub judice principle would be equally applied to all Articles of Impeachment leveled against Vice President Sara Duterte, including the three that were…

blocks.text: Published November 6, 2026 10:14am

The Senate impeachment court has ruled that the sub judice principle would be equally applied to all Articles of Impeachment leveled against Vice President Sara Duterte, including the three that were dropped by the prosecution.

In an order signed by presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero, the impeachment court resolved that the sub judice principle under Rule 18 of the Rules of Procedure on impeachment trials shall apply “with equal force” to all articles of impeachment, whether withdrawn or pending adjudication.

This, after the defense panel filed a manifestation on November 4, stating that Duterte is not waiving Rule 18 and that the impeachment court must maintain and enforce the sub judice rule “to preserve the integrity of the proceedings and ensure that her constitutional rights are respected.”

On August 26, Escudero issued a ruling barring senator-judges, as well as counsels of both the prosecution and the defense, from speaking on the merits of the impeachment case against the Vice President.

This is in compliance with Article 18 of the Rules on Impeachment which provides that the presiding officer, the members of the Senate, “shall refrain from making any comments and disclosures in public pertaining to the merits of a pending impeachment trial” and that “the same shall likewise apply to the prosecutors, the person impeached, and their respective counsel and witnesses.”

The impeachment court, in the latest order, upheld and reiterated the August 26 ruling and enjoined all persons covered to refrain from making, issuing, or promoting any public statement or commentary concerning the merits of the pending trial or any matter encompassed by the Articles of Impeachment.
The court stressed that any violation of the directive shall be dealt with in accordance with the penalty system under the guidelines set by the ruling.

During the trial on October 13, the House prosecution panel dropped three out of the four Articles of Impeachment leveled against the Vice President, saying its case would stand on Article II alone on alleged unexplained wealth due to non-full declaration of assets and non-divestment of business.

The withdrawn impeachment articles were: Article I on confidential funds, Article III on bribery, and Article IV on assassination plot, grave threats, and inciting to sedition against President Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former Speaker Martin Romualdez. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon tells double murder trial shooting of Jesse Baird wasn’t intentional but ‘it was my fault’
articles.summary: Former NSW police officer gives evidence for a second day after pleading not guilty to murdering Baird and Luke Davies in early 2024

blocks.text: Beau Lamarre-Condon has said he is “guilty of manslaughter” but said shooting Jesse Baird wasn’t intentional, as he gave evidence in his double-murder trial.
The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
Lamarre-Condon continued giving evidence at the New South Wales supreme court on Friday. He described the moment he shot Baird, at which point Baird’s mother, Helen, left the courtroom.
“As police officers we are trained to shoot people at the centre of body mass … I had a split second moment where I said drop the knife … It was just police mode now,” he said from the witness box.
“If I didn’t do that I was 110% going to have that knife driven into my throat. And Jesse Baird was going to be sitting in my position today.”

blocks.caption: Luke Davies (left) and Jesse Baird (right). Composite: Supplied/NSW Supreme Court

blocks.text: He told the jury about an occasion when he went to the Royal national park with a friend and shot his gun. At this time he was thinking of taking his own life, and he wanted to test how loud his gun was, he told the jury.
He says he fired it at a tree. “I was very aware of making sure the bullet didn’t hit any innocent person,” Lamarre-Condon said.
The court also heard Lamarre-Condon signed out his firearm for a shift, three days before the alleged murders.
He had permission to do this, he told the court, and on the way to work had stopped at East Village shopping centre in Zetland to get his car washed.
The former officer claimed in court that it was common for police to get coffee or stop off elsewhere on the way to work.

He said he was thinking of stopping at Paddington to get his belongings from Baird before the other man got home from work, which would have put him in the “exact same” position he was in today as his firearm was still in his backpack.
On the day of the alleged murders, the officer said he wanted to retrieve his surfboard, clothes and Cartier ring from Baird’s home.
He took his mother’s car, because he did not want to be recognised, and began driving up and down Baird’s street to look for his ute, the jury heard.
Lamarre-Condon then parked the car in a spot left by Baird’s housemate, he told the jury.

He claimed he did not want to come into contact with Baird due to a risk the other man could take out an apprehended violence order against him as Baird had previously asked him to “please refrain from contacting me”.
Lamarre-Condon told the court he had seen what he assumed to be someone’s delivery motorcycle: “As soon as I saw that I had an idea … I saw a hi-vis hooded jacket, waterproof long pants and gloves.

“This moment here … I wish that I didn’t do this … But I had the thought process that if I was to put on this helmet and outfit I could knock on Jesse’s door I would look like an UberEats driver without any verbal interaction with Jesse,” he said.
The accused claimed Baird’s room was empty when he entered the home and that he looked through some storage boxes in the bedroom in search of his clothes but couldn’t find them.
Lamarre-Condon said he was still wearing the motorcycle helmet and his firearm in a holster under his shirt, when Baird saw him.
“He started yelling, ‘we’re getting robbed, we’re getting robbed’ … He couldn’t see it was me because the visor was down,” Lamarre-Condon said.
after newsletter promotion
At this point he claimed Baird lunged at him.
Lamarre-Condon claimed he aimed for Baird’s right shoulder and discharged the firearm.
The two continued to struggle but the officer’s finger remained on the trigger, the jury heard.

They tripped over a storage box on the ground, which is when Lamarre-Condon “accidentally” discharged the gun, he told the court: “It was my fault … I am guilty of manslaughter… But it wasn’t intentional.”
The jury heard he dialled the emergency hotline to try to get help for Baird.
But when he looked up, he saw Davies, who he didn’t recognise him at the time.
The accused claims the other man had picked up his gun.
“It was pointed towards me at my chest and he said ‘I’m going to fucking shoot you’,” he told the court.
“I started lowering my body towards the ground: I said, ‘Please don’t shoot me, I’m not here to shoot you. I’m not a threat I’m not here to hurt you.’
“That’s when he raised the gun towards my head and said, ‘Fuck off.”
The former officer said police are trained to redirect gun muzzles when firearms are pointed at them.
“I saw the gun, he was holding it with both hands I thought fuck he’s going to fire the gun and that’s where my police training kicked in,” he told the court.
“My left hand would have grabbed Luke’s left wrist and turned it away … my other hand pushed against the forearm and then I pushed the pivot point of the left wrist away from me.”
Asked by the defence lawyer whether the gun went off, Lamarre-Condon says:
“Yes, during this motion. And it got Luke.”
The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.

articles.title: Peru airport officials discover 3,000 tarantulas smuggled inside dirty socks
articles.summary:
Three suitcases’ worth of the spiders were on their way to Germany, where they could fetch an estimated €1.5m

More than 3,000 tarantulas were seized at an airport in Lima on their way to…

blocks.text: More than 3,000 tarantulas were seized at an airport in Lima on their way to Germany, Peruvian authorities said.

The spiders were hidden inside dirty socks contained in three suitcases carried by two Germans and a Polish citizen, the National Forestry and Wildlife Service (SERFOR) told Agence France-Presse on Thursday.

They were spotted after agents noticed some unusual wriggling inside the luggage during a routine customs inspection at Jorge Chávez international airport. “We noticed that some of them were moving. There were small ones and large ones,” said Cora Suarez, a SERFOR wildlife control technician.

blocks.caption: The hatchlings were hidden inside a sock.   Photograph: SERFOR/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: One tarantula can sell for about €500 ($560) in Europe, Suarez said, meaning the wildlife trafficking scheme would be potentially worth €1.5m for just one trip.
The hidden arachnids, which came from several regions of Peru, were found in varying stages of development, from eggs and hatchlings to adults, Suarez said.
The Europeans accused of smuggling the tarantulas were detained by police specialising in environmental crimes and will face criminal proceedings, SERFOR said.
Illegal wildlife trafficking is a highly lucrative criminal activity that generates around $20bn annually worldwide, according to Interpol.
Such trafficking is among the primary causes of the loss of biodiversity on the planet.

articles.title: Hontiveros questions Joseph Sy's absence at Senate hearing
articles.summary: Senator Risa Hontiveros on Friday questioned businessman Joseph Sy's absence from a Senate hearing on Thursday after he reportedly went to the emergency room of a hospital due to health concerns.

blocks.text: Published November 6, 2026 9:21am
Senator Risa Hontiveros on Friday questioned businessman Joseph Sy's absence from a Senate hearing on Thursday after he reportedly went to the emergency room of a hospital due to health concerns.
Interviewed on GMA News' Unang Balita, Hontiveros said Sy had allegedly attended a party a couple of weeks earlier to celebrate his release on bail.
"Kung kaya naman pala niya mag-party, kaya naman niya sigurong dumalo muli kahit minsan pa sa Senado para humarap sa aming komite," the senator said.
(If he can party, he can probably come to the Senate at least once more to appear before our committee.)

Despite Sy’s absence, Hontiveros said several government agencies that attended the hearing committed to reviewing their databases and strengthening coordination to prevent foreigners from exploiting Philippine identity documents and government systems.

These include the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), Office of the Solicitor General (OSG), Bureau of Immigration (BI), and Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA).
Hontiveros said the agencies would conduct internal audits and improve information-sharing to address the alleged use of fraudulent Philippine birth certificates and passports by foreign nationals.

She said some foreigners had allegedly abused the late registration of birth certificates to acquire Filipino identities and engage in businesses with regulations on foreign ownership, including mining.
“Si Joseph Sy naging pangulo ng isang malaking Philippine mining company. Nailuwas niya ang ating mga likas na yaman at doon siya yumaman,” she said.
(Joseph Sy became the president of a large Philippine mining company. He exported our natural resources and that's where he got rich.)
During Thursday's hearing, PSA said it found evidence showing that the embattled businessman procured fake documents during his birth registration process.
Suspected of being a Chinese national posing as a Filipino, Sy was arrested by Philippine authorities in 2025 when he arrived at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport from Hong Kong.
The Supreme Court (SC) First Division ordered last month the release of Sy, ruling in favor of his petition for habeas corpus.
The Bureau of Immigration (BI) said it respected the SC’s resolution on the petition, but clarified that the Court did not settle the matter of Sy’s nationality.
Meanwhile, Hontiveros also warned about the continued operations of illegal POGOs, which she described as having transformed into "guerrilla POGOs" following the passage of the Anti-POGO Act.
She said these groups may also be involved in scam operations and troll farms spreading disinformation, posing a broader threat to national security and Philippine democracy. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Trump signs order preventing future presidents from changing Oval Office
articles.summary: The order comes after Trump made a series of big changes the Oval Office decor and launched landmark construction projects across Washington.

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order that he says will prevent future presidents from making certain changes to the White House Oval Office.
Trump, a former real estate mogul, has altered the president's official office during his second term, most notably by adding many gold features to its walls.

"So we're making it a national monument, and it will not be allowed to be touched by anybody, destroyed, ripped down by stupid people, in order to build something in a slightly different shape," Trump told reporters on Thursday.
American presidents currently have the power to make some changes to the White House but large projects require the permission of Congress.
Thursday's executive order declares the Oval Office to be a national monument, along with some of its surrounding rooms.

The document also says that it does not "restrict the President's authority to redecorate the monument, select furnishings, or make ordinary operational and security modifications that do not substantially impair the monument's historic structure or architectural character".
"We like the Oval Office, and it's a symbol like the White House itself. It's a symbol of our country and the greatness of our country," Trump said.

items: How Trump is remaking the White House in his own image

blocks.text: The president has the power to create national monuments, which are similar to national parks.
Trump's order calls on the office to be maintained by the National Park Service "in a manner that protects its historic character, architectural integrity, and association with the Presidency".
The entire building is already designated as a National Historic Landmark, which is intended to prevent against sudden changes to the building.

Trump's proclamation notes the existing protection, but says "nonetheless, the Oval Office merits specific recognition and protective management as a discrete historic structure of national significance".

Congress has carved out an exemption to the National Historic Preservation Act, in order to allow presidents to make needed changes. The current Oval Office has existed since the early 1930s, after its conception by President Franklin D Roosevelt.

Greg Werkheiser, from the law firm Cultural Heritage Partners, which specialises in historic preservation, says that temporary alterations like "furniture and decor is completely up to the president's discretion".
"As long as they're not damaging the permanent art and architecture, they can generally do whatever they want," he tells BBC News.
Werkheiser argues that the Trump administration has shown extreme disregard for other historic sites in Washington, and through lawsuits has attempted to undermine the laws that require preservation.

Trump has undertaken a massive beautification project in Washington and has held three events in the past week to boast of the construction, even as his Republican party was trounced by Democrats in the midterm elections.

"The hypocrisy is that on the one hand he's talking about the importance of preserving the Oval Office - which is legally meaningless because he can't do it - and on the other hand he is absolutely taking an axe to the law that allows us to preserve other historic sites."

Werkheiser notes Trump's efforts to renovate the Kennedy Center in Washington DC, to build a new triumphal arch in the city, and to paint the granite exterior of the historic executive office building. His firm has filed lawsuits to block two of the projects.
In October, the president suggested in an interview with Time, external magazine that the Oval Office would need to be torn down due to security concerns from the US Secret Service.
"I said, 'My ass, you can't build a new one. This is a special place,'" Trump said at the time.

During the midterm election campaign Democrats criticised Trump's redesigns, with former President Barack Obama saying that his golden tweaks have "got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory".

articles.title: Risa Hontiveros bares possible red flags in proposed 2027 budget
articles.summary: Senator Risa Hontiveros on Friday identified possible budget items that could raise red flags during the Senate's deliberations on the proposed 2027 national budget.

blocks.text: Published November 6, 2026 8:46am
Senator Risa Hontiveros on Friday identified possible budget items that could raise red flags during the Senate's deliberations on the proposed 2027 national budget.

Hontiveros said she would push for sufficient funding for the full implementation of universal healthcare through the Department of Health (DOH) and the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth).

“Ang magiging red flag sa ganitong mga budgets ay kung babawasan halimbawa 'yung budget ng DOH para sa immunization o di kaya para sa patuloy na pagbuo ng health facilities system dito sa ating bansa,” she told GMA News’ Unang Balita in an interview.
(What would be a red flag in these budgets is if the DOH budget for immunization or for the continued development of the health facilities system here in our country is reduced.)
Hontiveros also warned against removing the government's counterpart funding for foreign-assisted projects.
She recalled that such funding had previously been removed and transferred to unprogrammed appropriations, calling it “problematic.”
The senator said the government should avoid repeating previous budget allocation errors amid ongoing investigations into alleged irregularities in flood control projects.

Hontiveros, who is sponsoring the budgets of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), also said she would push for adequate funding for their programs.

“Isusulong ko talaga na maging Super El Niño-ready at responsive ang DENR budget. At gayundin para sa DSWD budget na masuportahan 'yung mga magagandang programa nila tulad ng LAWA at BINHI na isang programa na parehong tungkol sa water development at conservation at livelihood din,” she said.

(I will really push for the DENR budget to be Super El Niño-ready and responsive. And the same goes for the DSWD budget to support their great programs like LAWA and BINHI, which are programs that are both about water development and conservation and livelihood as well.)

Meanwhile, Hontiveros said the Senate had so far identified around P7 billion worth of budget line items, programs, activities, and projects that lacked sufficient supporting documents or justification.
These included items without a program of works, letters of request, resolutions, ordinances, or approval from local development councils.
She said senators were committed to continuing budget reforms, including opening budget hearings to civil society groups and allowing greater public participation in the budget process.—AOL, GMA News

articles.title: [Puso at Diwa] Wanted: Integrity dividend
articles.summary: The Philippines does not need another political savior. It needs an integrity dividend.

blocks.text: The flood control scandal, the investigations involving powerful political figures, the impending arrest of Senator Bato de la Rosa, and the impeachment proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte may appear to be separate political developments. But they raise one fundamental question: Can the Philippines finally move beyond political personalities and confront the deeper problems of corruption, weak institutions and poor governance?
This is not just a political question. It is an economic one.

At a time when the economy needs more investment, stronger consumer spending and renewed business confidence, the country is caught in a cycle of political controversy and institutional uncertainty. The consequences are being felt not only in government but also in businesses, households and the broader economy.

Consider what is happening. The economy grew by only 2.3% in the second quarter of 2026. More troubling, investment declined by 9.2%. Household consumption continued to grow, but at a slower pace of 2.8%, extending a four-quarter slowdown.

These numbers have several explanations, including surging inflation, higher borrowing costs and persistent external shocks. But governance and political uncertainty are also part of the problem. And we should not underestimate their economic cost.
The flood control anomalies have exposed how public funds intended to protect communities from flooding and disasters may have been wasted or diverted through questionable projects and contracts.
The damage goes far beyond the money allegedly lost.

Every peso wasted on an overpriced, substandard or nonexistent project is a peso that could have built a better road, protected a community, improved a school or supported a hospital. When flood control projects fail, families lose homes and livelihoods, businesses suffer disruptions, and farmers lose crops. The economy pays repeatedly for infrastructure that should have protected it in the first place.
This is why accountability matters. Investigations, audits and the filing of cases against those implicated are necessary. No public official or contractor should be above the law.
But catching the people responsible is only half the job. We must also change the system that allowed these things to happen.

How can questionable projects pass through government approval? Why are procurement and project monitoring safeguards inadequate? Why can public funds be allocated without sufficiently transparent and independent scrutiny?
Unless these questions are answered, the country risks repeating the same scandal under different names and political personalities.
The impeachment proceedings against the Vice President present another test of our democratic institutions.

blocks.caption: [Puso at Diwa] Sara Duterte trial: Is the space for political impunity finally closing?

blocks.text: The issue should not be whether one belongs to the administration or the opposition, or whether one enjoys greater political support. The issue is whether constitutional processes are followed fairly, transparently and consistently.

The same standards must apply to everyone implicated in corruption allegations, regardless of political position or affiliation. The presumption of innocence and the right to due process must be respected. Impeachment must be decided on constitutional and evidentiary grounds, not political alliance or convenience.
There is a danger that these proceedings will become another contest between political factions, with each side more concerned about winning power than strengthening institutions.

If people come to believe that investigations and impeachment are simply weapons used against political opponents, public trust will suffer further. Even legitimate efforts to establish accountability can lose credibility when they are perceived as selective or partisan.
The country needs justice, not political revenge. It needs accountability, not another round of political score-settling.
Why should ordinary Filipinos care about these political and institutional developments?
Because confidence matters to economic activity.

Businesses invest when they believe the rules are predictable, contracts will be honored, government policies will be consistent and public institutions can be trusted. When uncertainty rises, businesses hesitate. They postpone expansion, delay purchases of equipment, defer hiring and sometimes move their investments elsewhere.

Households behave similarly. When people worry about their jobs, incomes, prices and the country’s economic direction, they become more cautious. They postpone buying a house, a car or appliances. They reduce discretionary spending and save more for emergencies.

When businesses invest less and households spend less, economic activity weakens. Companies earn less, employment opportunities become limited, and government collects less revenue. This can reinforce the very economic difficulties that created the uncertainty in the first place.

This is the connection between governance and the everyday lives of Filipinos. Corruption and political instability are not abstract problems confined to Congress, Malacañang or government agencies. They affect jobs, incomes, prices, public services and opportunities.
The cost of corruption is not only the money stolen. It is also the investment that never happens, the job that is never created and the economic opportunity that is lost.

blocks.caption: Flood control corruption cleanup spooks investors, drags PH growth – World Bank

blocks.text: Perhaps the most difficult truth is that Philippine politics remains heavily driven by personalities, political dynasties, patronage and narrow vested interests.
Political alliances change, personalities rise and fall, and elections rearrange the balance of power. But the underlying incentives often remain the same.

We cannot expect meaningful transformation simply by replacing one group of politicians with another of their kind. Unless we reform the way political power is exercised and public money is allocated, the same problems will return.

We need more transparent political financing, stronger procurement safeguards, independent auditing, meaningful legislative oversight and greater public access to information about government spending.

The budget process itself deserves serious reform. Public funds must be allocated according to clear national priorities and measurable economic and social benefits, not political accommodation. The 2027 national budget provides an immediate opportunity to demonstrate that government has learned from the flood control scandal.

Political dynasties and the concentration of political power should also be squarely addressed, as contemplated by the Constitution. Ultimately, public office must be treated as a responsibility to serve, not an opportunity to accumulate power and resources.

blocks.caption: [Puso at Diwa] Anti-political dynasties: When democracy belongs to the people

blocks.text: There is an argument that aggressively pursuing corruption cases and confronting political controversies could further unsettle the economy. There may indeed be short-term costs when questionable projects are suspended, government spending is reviewed and powerful political interests are challenged.
But avoiding accountability in the name of economic stability would be a much greater mistake.

The solution is not to abandon investigations or compromise justice. It is to ensure that accountability is pursued fairly, efficiently and without political interference, while legitimate public investments and essential services continue.

The Philippines needs what may be called an integrity dividend: the benefits that come when people trust government, public funds are used properly, businesses feel secure investing, and households believe that the future is worth preparing for.

This dividend cannot be produced simply by arresting a few prominent personalities or removing one political figure from office. It requires institutions that work regardless of who occupies public office.

The real measure of success is not only about how many politicians are investigated, arrested or impeached. It is also about how public money is better spent, government services improve, businesses invest with greater confidence, and ordinary Filipinos enjoy more opportunities.
The country does not need another political savior. It needs a political and economic system that does not depend on saviors in the first place.
Good governance is not an obstacle to economic growth. It is one of its most important foundations. And when governance fails, it is ultimately the ordinary Filipinos who pay the price. – Rappler.com

Diwa C. Guinigundo is the former deputy governor for monetary policy and other aspects of central banking. He was a former alternate executive director at the IMF in Washington, DC in 2001-2003. He is the author and editor of several books on political economy, regional crisis and cooperation, debt and economic growth and public policy agenda.
He serves as independent director of several corporate and financial institutions with focus on corporate governance, risk oversight and audit.

He also serves as principal advisor for New York-based GlobalSourcePartners. He remains in the advisory board of ASEAN Macroeconomic Research Office and Singapore Management University’s Sim Kee Boon Institute for Financial Economics.
He is the senior pastor of the Fullness of Christ International Ministries in Mandaluyong.

articles.title: Trump declares his redesigned Oval Office a national monument
articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump signed a proclamation Thursday declaring the Oval Office and Cabinet room of the White House to be national monuments.

image.caption: U.S. President Donald Trump signed a proclamation Thursday declaring the Oval Office and the Cabinet room of the White House to be national monuments, which he said will prevent future administrations from making significant modifications. (Alex Brandon/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World
U.S. President Donald Trump signed a proclamation Thursday declaring the Oval Office and Cabinet room of the White House to be national monuments.
In week of midterm thumping, Trump holds 3rd event focused on a Washington renovation project
U.S. President Donald Trump signed a proclamation Thursday declaring the Oval Office and Cabinet room of the White House to be preserved as national monuments.

Trump said his proclamation will prevent future presidents from making major changes to the two White House rooms — which he has extensively redecorated since the start of his second term — without the approval of Congress.

"It will make it impossible for anybody ever to destroy this incredible space," he told reporters in the Oval Office. "It will not be allowed to be touched by anybody, destroyed, ripped down by stupid people."

Even though the White House is designated a National Historic Landmark, Trump has demolished its East Wing to build a new ballroom, paved over the Rose Garden and built a concrete helipad on the South Lawn, all since his return to the presidency last year and without Congressional approval.

In a week when Trump's Republican Party suffered a dramatic smackdown in the midterm elections, this was the third day in which the president has made one of his Washington, D.C. renovation projects the central subject of his media event.
On Wednesday, he took the White House press pool to the ballroom site and put his signature on a concrete beam.
Trump has overseen a gold-tinged redecoration of the Oval Office interior. (Alex Brandon/The Associated Press)
On Monday, the final day of the midterm campaign, he gave a speech to mark the conclusion of the problem-plagued renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.
Trump's declaration of the Oval Office and Cabinet room as national monuments was his first official presidential action since the midterm loss.
'Of great interest to me'
He called the move "something that is of great interest to me, but it's of great interest to a lot of people."

As Trump signed the proclamation, a red baseball cap with "VETO" in white letters sat on his desk. The U.S. president has the power to veto legislation that falls short of a two-thirds majority in either the House or the Senate.

items: Trump 'out of touch with reality' about midterm losses, says Republican strategist
What the Republican midterm defeat means for Trump, the U.S. and Canada

blocks.text: Trump's focus on renovations is raising questions about his political priorities, particularly in light of the drubbing the Republicans took in the midterms.
His Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress, only the third time that has happened to a sitting president's party during a midterm election in the past 80 years.
A view of the Oval Office on Jan. 20, 2021, the first day of then-president Joe Biden's term in office. (Alex Brandon/The Associated Press)

The Democratic Party flipped seven GOP Senate seats, including from deep red states such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. The Democrats won at least 253 Congressional districts, putting them on track for the biggest House margin that any party has held since 1990.
Key Republicans have been quick to point fingers over the midterm loss.

items: JD Vance blames Iran war for midterm thumping. Is he really blaming Trump?
Ohio and Texas went from red to blue in the midterms but may not stay that way in 2028

blocks.text: Texas Sen. Ted Cruz blamed the election loss on elected Republicans dismissing voters' concerns about the cost of living.
"Tariffs have made everything too expensive, and the Iran war has dragged on too long," Cruz said Wednesday on his podcast Verdict.
"Too many Republican politicians seem like they didn’t understand or they didn’t care,” he said.
Earlier Wednesday, U.S. Vice-President JD Vance blamed the results on the war in Iran, while Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said Republican messaging didn't address the real concerns of voters.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Mike Crawley is a correspondent for CBC News, based in Washington. He began his career as a newspaper reporter in B.C., spent six years as a freelance journalist in various parts of Africa, then joined the CBC in 2005. Mike reported on Ontario politics for 15 years. He was born and raised in Saint John, N.B.

articles.title: Trump signs proclamation to try to prevent changes to gold-covered Oval Office
articles.summary:
President seeks to make Oval Office a national monument to ensure designs are not ‘ripped down by stupid people’

Donald Trump signed a proclamation on Thursday that he says will prevent…

blocks.text: Donald Trump signed a proclamation on Thursday that he says will prevent future administrations from changing his design of the Oval Office and Cabinet Room, spaces which he declared as national monuments that should be preserved.

In the days since his party suffered historic defeats in the midterm elections, the president has seemingly turned his attention to the many renovation projects he has begun across the nation’s capital. Sitting behind the Resolute Desk on Thursday, Trump declared the Oval Office a “national monument”.
“I’m going to be signing a document which will make them into a landmark for the ages,” he told reporters in the gold-covered Oval Office.

According to the president, the proclamation would ensure the West Wing rooms would not be “touched by anybody, destroyed, ripped down by stupid people, in order to build something in a slightly different shape”.
“I just thought it was very important that nobody be allowed to come and take it down and try and do something with it,” he said.

“Every once in a while they’ll look and they’ll say, oh, maybe what we’ll do is we’ll put some glass up that’s a little bit better or something, and I say no, you’re not going to do anything. We’re going to leave this as it is,” he continued.
“If anyone ever decides to come and start knocking down walls, you’ll call me wherever I may be, and I will come back here and I will make sure it never happens.”

Since returning to office, Trump has embarked on a series of White House “beautification” projects, most notably the demolition of the East Wing to make way for a $600m ballroom, as well the building of a permanent granite helipad on the South Lawn.

Speaking to reporters from the Oval Office, the president defended his wider renovation work at the White House, saying the building’s exterior had suffered from years of deterioration. He pointed to cracked windows, damaged stonework and broken decorative features, saying he had paid for repairs and hired skilled workers to restore them.
“When you looked at that wall one year ago, it was badly damaged from years of service,” he said, adding that exterior columns had also been in “horrible shape”.

On the desk next to where he signed the proclamation was a red baseball cap emblazoned with the word “Veto” – an explicit reminder of his threat to block the legislative priorities and bills passed by the new Democratic-controlled Congress next year.

blocks.caption: The baseball hat with ‘Veto’ written on the front. Photograph: Shawn Thew-Pool/CNP/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Democrats made significant gains in several traditionally Republican states where Trump had previously won, including Texas, Kansas, South Carolina and Iowa, by campaigning on issues including affordability and tackling corruption, while also securing control of Congress.

Trump’s opulent redesign of the Oval Office has drawn criticism, including from former president Barack Obama, who recently joked that “he’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory. Just gold everywhere.”
Obama’s remark prompted a coordinated response from the White House, with treasury secretary Scott Bessent appearing to hit back by dining at a Cheesecake Factory.

In a final appeal ahead of the midterm elections, Trump held a press conference highlighting the delayed results of his $14m renovation of the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool, while blaming Joe Biden for the algae that had accumulated in its waters.
“This was in the Biden era … Look, it’s not an easy thing. The algae is brutal. It forms easily. All you saw was dirt and filth and paper and everything else for years,” Trump said on Monday.
Two days later, as the scale of his party’s staggering losses came into focus, Trump led a media tour of the White House Ballroom construction site, where he marveled at the renovations to come.
“The whole thing is a miracle,” he said.

articles.title: Slashing number of police forces in England and Wales is only option, says Met chief
articles.summary:
Mark Rowley calls for ‘revolution’ in policing as major review is expected to propose regional ‘super forces’

Police are heading for failure unless the number of forces in England and Wales…
articles.byline: Vikram Dodd Police and crime correspondent

blocks.text: Police are heading for failure unless the number of forces in England and Wales is slashed, with their ability to catch criminals collapsing and public confidence falling, Britain’s top officer will say on Friday.
The stark comments from Sir Mark Rowley, the commissioner of the Metropolitan police, come as some police leaders demand a radical package of reforms.
An official review ordered by the government has concluded that the number of police forces in England should be cut from 39 to as few as nine “super forces”, according to multiple sources.
The review, carried out by the former Met police commissioner Bernard Hogan-Howe, is yet to be published.

Sources say that under consideration is the establishment of nine regional forces, plus a single force for Wales, which would sit above more than 150 local policing units that would deliver most neighbourhood crime-fighting activities.

The axing of most of the 43 forces in England and Wales is seen as essential by the Hogan-Howe review and some police chiefs. Those chiefs, including Rowley, are concerned that the government may delay the most radical change to policing in seven decades.

Hogan-Howe’s review was completed in September and sent to the home secretary, Shabana Mahmood. Government sources say only that it will be published before Christmas, with a white paper due in the new year.
The delay is understood to be because of Andy Burnham’s devolution agenda and desire to “rewire” the British state and reform local government, including adding more mayors.

blocks.caption: Shabana Mahmood speaks with police officers during a walkabout in Lambeth, south London, in January. Photograph: James Manning/PA

blocks.text: One police source said: “There are some concerns Andy Burnham may want to align the new police structures with mayors, which could mean 20 or more forces. That is not a radical enough change.”
Rowley will speak at an event in Manchester on Friday where he and other chiefs including Greater Manchester’s chief constable, Sir Stephen Watson, will press for a reduction in the number of forces.

The event’s title is “The cost of standing still is that criminals will win”. Some other chief constables have told the Guardian they are annoyed by the Met-organised event and are sceptical or do not support the big reduction down to nine forces.

Cutting the number of forces in England and Wales is the centrepiece of Mahmood’s radical changes to policing. Hogan-Howe’s report, multiple sources say, gives a range of how many larger forces there should be in the new policing landscape, from nine to 18.

Rowley will say in his speech that public confidence has already fallen and that positive outcomes – that is, crimes detected by officers that lead to a charge, caution, out of court settlement or no further action – “are now less than half what they were 12 years ago”.

According to extracts released before the speech, Rowley will say: “I believe this is a choice between the third greatest revolution in British policing or the inevitable decline and fewer bobbies on the beat.”

He will say the 43 forces in England and Wales should be cut to eight or 10, and add: “Policing has tried to keep up, made do as best it can to patch over our broken model … But the model is creaking. We have 43 overstretched forces trying to do too much with too little.”

blocks.caption: Sir Mark Rowley, the Met commissioner, will say there are 43 forces ‘trying to do too much with too little’. Photograph: Thomas Krych/Story Picture Agency/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Hogan-Howe believes the changes would free up policing to rapidly innovate as new crime types and threats emerge. The 43 forces model, overseen by 43 police and crime commissioners, is accused of being too slow and delivering a postcode lottery of varying service for crime victims.
Hogan-Howe came out publicly in favour of a reduction to nine forces 12 years ago.

The bigger forces would handle major crimes – such as murders and serious sexual violence – and public order, as well as expensive but essential back-office functions such as human resources, currently done by each of the 43 forces individually.

Above the regional forces would sit a new nationwide force called the National Police Service, which the government wants to be the home of counter-terrorism policing and serious and organised crime. The advert for a commissioner for the national force is expected to be issued early in the new year.

There is division among police leaders about the big reduction in forces. Some favour voluntary mergers, and the new white paper will allow the mass abolition of forces and creation of new ones to be enforced.

The changes could lead to a vast south-east England force stretching from the London borders to the southern coast of England. A new north-west force would extend from the Mersey to the Pennines, covering Greater Manchester, Merseyside and Lancashire, as well as swallowing up smaller forces such as Cheshire and Cumbria.
One chief constable told the Guardian: “Everyone knows 43 forces have to go. But the return on investment could take five or six years.”
Another chief constable said: “If I was the chief constable of the super force, it would be such a huge area, I wouldn’t know anybody. I worry about it being too big.”

Matthew Scott, the Conservative police and crime commissioner for Kent, said: “They will spend a great deal of time tearing up the fabric of policing for a suboptimal outcome.” The government plans to abolish PCCs as part of its changes.

Another police leader asked: “Where is the evidence bigger forces are better?” They cited the fact that in recent years the largest – such as the Met, Greater Manchester and West Midlands – had failed so badly they had been put into special measures and their chief constables or commissioners had been ousted.
Scotland and Northern Ireland are each already covered by a single force.

articles.title: Pope begins lengthy trip to Latin America weeks after lung cancer surgery
articles.summary: Pope Leo, who had part of a lung removed last month, will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

blocks.text: Pope begins lengthy trip to Latin America weeks after lung cancer surgery
Image source, Reuters
Pope Leo is travelling to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru
BySarah Rainsford
Southern and Eastern Europe correspondent, Rome

Pope Leo XIV is beginning a lengthy trip to Latin America just three weeks after surgery for lung cancer - a tour that includes a much-anticipated "homecoming" to Peru where he was a priest for many years.

The Vatican says no extraordinary measures are being taken in relation to the Pope's health, describing him as a "71-year-old who has undergone an operation" not someone with a "permanent medical condition".

It was Leo himself who revealed last month that doctors had discovered a tumour during a routine scan. The growth was removed along with the lower lobe of his right lung and his medical team then confirmed the cancer had not spread.

At a briefing in Rome ahead of the trip, which takes in Uruguay and Argentina as well as Peru, a spokeswoman stressed that Pope Leo had "fantastic stamina" and was "extremely enthusiastic" about the schedule which he had "personally confirmed... with no changes".
Back on track

"The Vatican's message with this trip is, 'that was a short episode and now we're back on track'," Professor Massimo Faggioli of Villanova University told the BBC, pointing out that the Pope has had a busy return to work since his surgery.
"We have seen him in these last few days making speeches, audiences and so on. He seems in great shape. That was important."

blocks.caption: Image caption, On Friday Pope Leo presided over the annual memorial Mass for cardinals and bishops who have died

blocks.text: Image source, EPA
On Friday Pope Leo presided over the annual memorial Mass for cardinals and bishops who have died
The 12-day tour would be demanding for anyone, though. It incorporates multiple long-haul and local flights and covers thousands of miles from the Amazon to the Andes.
The starting point will be Uruguay, where the number of Catholics has fallen away steeply in recent years and which is getting its first Papal visit in four decades.
Leo then heads for Argentina, homeland of Pope Francis, his predecessor.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Father Fernando Laguna said his heart was filled with joy when the Pope's visit to Argentina was announced

blocks.text: Father Fernando Laguna said his heart was filled with joy when the Pope's visit to Argentina was announced
"This visit is also a homage to Francis, who didn't make it to Argentina [as pope]," says Father Fernando Laguna, the rector of Santa Maria Addolorata, Argentina's national church in Rome.

"When this visit by Pope Leo was announced, it filled all of our hearts with joy," he told the BBC. "I always thought he would go, despite his illness. I don't think he ever thought of calling it off!"

The priest is installing a big screen inside the church in Rome to allow parishioners to follow all the key moments of the trip from afar. The building is already decked out with posters declaring Pope Leo is welcome in Argentina. "We're waiting for you!", one proclaims.

blocks.caption: Image caption, 'Welcome Pope Leo' reads this poster in the Argentinian church in Rome

blocks.text: 'Welcome Pope Leo' reads this poster in the Argentinian church in Rome

This leg of the Pope's journey - which includes meetings with heads of state as well as religious events - could be the most politically sensitive. President Javier Milei once called Pope Francis "evil on earth" and a "communist" for promoting a doctrine of social justice to help the poor. In turn, Argentina's bishops have criticised Milei's harsh austerity measures, making sweeping cuts to social spending.
But Milei has already welcomed Pope Leo, writing in a post on X that Argentina awaits "with immense joy". Millions are expected to turn out to greet him.
'Homecoming' to Peru
The highlight of the trip is undoubtedly saved for last, when Pope Leo reaches Peru - described by the Vatican as a return to his roots.
"He knows these streets," is how a spokeswoman put it.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Worshippers at Chiclayo cathedral in Peru were delighted when their former bishop became Pope in 2025

blocks.text: Worshippers at Chiclayo cathedral in Peru were delighted when their former bishop became Pope in 2025
Born in the US, the then Robert Prevost spent almost 20 years in Peru, on and off, and even has Peruvian citizenship. That time is seen as fundamental to shaping his papacy.
His schedule includes a return to the diocese of Chiclayo where he was ordained bishop in 2014 and remained until Francis moved him to the Vatican almost a decade later.
He will also travel to Cusco, former capital of the Inca Empire, to say Mass more than 3,000m above sea level before heading to Pucallpa in the Amazon.
In all three countries, the Vatican says the Pope will have meetings with survivors of clerical sexual abuse - an issue which clouded a 2018 visit to Chile and Peru by his predecessor.
"This is how the papacy reconnects with Latin America after Francis, whose visits to the region were not always seamless," is how Professor Faggioli sees it.
He believes Pope Leo has a strong sense of the unity of the Americas as one continent. "Democracies are in trouble there, so there are so many things he can address," he suggests.
"The big question then is the United States. There's no question he wants to go. So will he travel when [President Donald] Trump is still in office? I'm sure they're thinking about this."

articles.title: Florida puts man to death as three US executions scheduled for same day
articles.summary:
Indiana executed a man hours earlier, and in Alabama, a man was scheduled to die by injection later

Florida carried out a record-tying 19th execution of the year on Thursday in an unusual…

blocks.text: Florida and Alabama plan to execute one man each on Thursday just hours after Indiana put a prisoner to death – in the first of three lethal injections scheduled for the same day in the US.

It would be Florida’s 19th execution this year under the Republican governor, Ron DeSantis, matching a record set by the state in 2025, and the second time this year that three people would be put to death on the same day.

The death penalty in the US has faced renewed scrutiny since the September failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee, although courts have rejected efforts to halt other executions after she survived two massive doses of pentobarbital.
In Indiana on Thursday, Jeffrey Weisheit, 50, was pronounced dead at 12.45am at the state prison in Michigan City, said Noelle Russell, spokesperson at the state’s department of correction.

She said he had no final words. He had acknowledged killing his girlfriend’s two children in a house fire in the Evansville area in 2010 but had hoped that governor Mike Braun would grant clemency and change his sentence to life in prison. Braun declined.
Florida has carried out more than half the 32 executions in the US so far this year.

Jesse Guardado is set for execution later on Thursday after being convicted of fatally stabbing a 75-year-old woman inside her Walton county home in 2004 before stealing her jewelry box, $80 and other valuables to buy drugs. She had helped him get a job and housing. Guardado, now 64, had a court appeal turned down.

In Alabama, Michael Taylor is set to die by lethal injection on Thursday. In 1991, when he was 19, he beat two people, aged 83 and 79, to death with a metal bar during a robbery in their home in Gadsden.
Death penalty opponents had urged Alabama’s Republican governor, Kay Ivey, to reduce Taylor’s sentence to life in prison, but she declined.

Esther Brown of Project Hope to Abolish the Death Penalty said: “If the state kills Michael, it is not the 19-year-old who made the worst mistake of his life whom it kills. But the mature, well-respected, God-fearing man sitting in that cell today.”

The state plans to execute Taylor, 54, by lethal injection after a judge declared a nitrogen gas method unconstitutional. His attorneys objected to the last-minute switch to lethal injection since he selected nitrogen gas as his method several years ago, but a judge ruled against Taylor.

Alabama executed murderer Kenneth Smith in 2024 by nitrogen asphyxiation, in an episode that witnesses found excruciating, after previously failing to succeed in its attempt to kill him using lethal injection.

Meanwhile, in Indiana earlier on Thursday, lawyers failed to persuade the state governor to allow Weisheit to undergo brain scans to assess a history of head injuries and mental health problems. They had asked for a life sentence.

Weisheit’s last objection centered on the state’s planned use of lethal drugs purchased from a pharmacy that is facing a disciplinary hearing next week in front of the Indiana pharmacy board, the state regulatory agency.

The execution provided “long-awaited justice for Alyssa Lynch and her brother Caleb, two innocent children whose lives were stolen in an act of unspeakable cruelty”, Indiana attorney general Todd Rokita said.
The Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title: [Market Rider] Essential market insights on the recent GCash IPO
articles.summary: This newly proven playbook for market absorption could serve heavily as market strategies for upcoming mega-public offerings

blocks.text: Last month’s P60.9-billion GCash initial public offering (IPO) or more precisely of Mynt Inc., the parent company of GCash, was the largest in the history of the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE). It was also the biggest for Southeast Asia for 2026.

When the idea came out for the first time, many thought it was not possible. The market has been poor that it slowly but surely became the region’s bottom dweller in recent years. During this time, the PSE was said to “operate under a P30-billion domestic liquidity ceiling.” Public equity offerings exceeding this threshold routinely drained capital from other index stocks. It was suffering from a market structural anomaly where massive IPOs exhausted domestic liquidity, resulting in immediate post-listing price collapses. (READ: [Market Rider] Buy when there’s blood in the streets, even if it’s your own blood)

But the incredible happened. The IPO shattered local capital-raising records. The market withstood the stress test and presented an optimistic financial ecosystem for both present and future big ticket market debuts.
Let’s look at how it happened.

Essentially, the operational mechanics of the GCash debut offer definitive structural lessons in pricing discipline, liquidity management, and retail participation, fundamentally redrawing the blueprint for big-ticket public equity offerings. It also provided a glimpse into the local market’s actual capacity to absorb multi-billion-peso digital assets, frameworks that will directly dictate the strategy especially for future technology listings in the country.

Initially, the GCash IPO demonstrated that massive scale demands conservative pricing discipline; for in the past, large-cap listings on the PSE suffered from post-debut sell-offs due to overwhelming market supply.

In 2021, Monde Nissin maximized its valuation on day one by pricing at the absolute top of its range, leaving no “money on the table.” The resulting lack of a secondary market cushion triggered a multi-year valuation reset. Similarly, during its 2020 debut, Converge ICT resisted trimming its initial offer price despite pandemic-induced market volatility. When institutional selling intensified on Day 1, its local stabilization agent was forced to exhaust 85% of its defense fund within a fortnight just to establish a static floor.

True enough, even with the conservative anchoring, the trading price of GCash experienced a post-debut slump, hitting an intraday low of P5.95 or nearly 10% below offer on October 26. It required heavy post-IPO intervention from its stabilization agent (UBS) to steady the stock back to P6.61.

In this regard, GCash bypassed this market constraint through two distinct structural pillars. This is through the employment of a massive global cornerstone book and decentralized retail onboarding. GCash secured over 20 top-tier global cornerstone institutional investors, including BlackRock, Fidelity, HSBC, and Capital Group, who absorbed nearly 70% of the offered shares. This is now the new structural “floor” for new-economy tech stocks.

Conversely, by embedding the IPO natively into the GStocks PH platform, GCash unlocked an entirely new tier of retail investors. Over 140,000 everyday platform users collectively contributed P1.1 billion.

blocks.caption: Want to buy GCash shares? How retail investors can join the IPO

blocks.text: Unlike traditional day-traders who flip shares for short-term arbitrage, these platform-native users behaved as long-term, sticky collectors, effectively neutralizing immediate open-market selling pressure.
Out of this experience, global banking intervention and conservative initial pricing to withstand the local market’s finite depth are critical to meet the demands of a massive public equity offering.

Believe it or not, PSE’s decision to lower the minimum public float requirement to 12% for exceptionally large corporations like those valued over P200 billion or over, also helped contribute to the success of GCash’s IPO and listing. This reduction in the minimum requirement for public float has truly created a safer buffer against market exhaustion.

By also allowing modern tech infrastructure and fintech assets to trade on forward-looking growth multipliers, the PSE and the Securities Exchange Commission (SEC) have as well contributed to the successful IPO of GCash.

This newly proven playbook for market absorption could serve heavily as market strategies for upcoming mega-public offerings. However, it appears also has that the market cannot do it in rapid, localized succession without causing investor fatigue.

Recognizing this local capacity constraint, the regulators, issuers and underwriters may have to work more to remedy the problem by introducing a delicate balance of disciplined localized pricing, decentralized retail distribution, and forging a strategic bridge to global institutional capital. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Cavite pet crematorium contracted Bulacan couple to cremate pets — NBI
articles.summary: Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium in Bacoor, Cavite, contracted a married couple in San Jose del Monte City, Bulacan, to cremate dead pets entrusted to the establishment, the National Bureau of…

blocks.text: November 6, 2026 | 7:42am
A blurred image shows the remains of pets found inside plastic bags dumped along a roadside in San Jose del Monte City, Bulacan.
Luna and Furry Siblings via Facebook
Content warning: This article contains references to dumped animal remains.

MANILA, Philippines — Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium in Bacoor, Cavite, contracted a married couple in San Jose del Monte City, Bulacan, to cremate dead pets entrusted to the establishment, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) said on Thursday, November 5.

NBI Director Melvin Matibag said the Bacoor-based crematorium had initially ordered cremation equipment, but the machinery was never delivered, forcing the establishment to outsource the service to the couple.
The couple was supposed to cremate the animals and return their ashes to Ahjay Paws for release to their respective owners.
However, the couple allegedly could not accommodate the volume of dead pets sent to their facility and resorted to burying some of the remains instead of cremating them.

“Ang findings na natin dito, Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium, wala siyang facility, wala siyang equipment to do the cremation. So pinadala niya doon. Malaki 'yung volume ng dumarating,” Matibag said in an interview with GMA News.
(Our findings here: Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium had no facility or equipment to perform cremations, so the animals were sent there. A large volume was being delivered.)
Matibag said the couple eventually buried the animals, while some remains were dumped instead of being properly disposed of.
“So ang ginawa nila, linibing nila,” he added, citing the couple's testimony.
(So what they did was bury them.)

The dead animals were transported from Bacoor to San Jose del Monte City using a delivery courier service. Matibag said the courier was unaware that the packages contained animal remains because these were placed in sacks and plastic bags.
The couple surrendered to the NBI on Wednesday, November 4, and submitted statements detailing how the animals were handled. They also expressed willingness to testify in the investigation.

“We will help the Department of Justice identify who qualifies as a witness to further establish who has liabilities, but there is already a sworn statement based on the investigation of the Environmental Crime Division,” Matibag explained.
The NBI will forward the complaints to the Department of Justice, which will determine whether the couple may qualify as state witnesses.

The investigation follows the discovery of the remains of 26 dogs and three cats in plastic bags along a roadside in San Jose del Monte City on October 31. Bacoor City Mayor Strike Revilla ordered the closure of Ahjay Paws and directed the police to investigate its owner.
Matibag said a total of 49 dead pets had been linked to the couple, including those recently found in Bulacan.

The NBI will initially file six cases based on the complaints submitted to the bureau, with Matibag saying investigators already have sufficient evidence to bring the matter before the prosecutor's office.
The agency is also investigating possible violations of sanitation and environmental laws arising from the transportation and disposal of the animal remains.
The crematorium's management could also face estafa and violations of the Consumer Protection Act.
Meanwhile, around 250 pet owners are expected to file complaints against Ahjay Paws, according to earlier statements from local authorities.
