articles.title: Pet crematorium enlisted bystanders to bury dead dogs and cats in Bulacan
articles.summary: The owners of a pet crematorium involved in the controversial dumping of pet remains in San Jose Del Monte (SJDM), Bulacan have surfaced, admitting that they enlisted the help of bystanders or…

blocks.text: Published November 6, 2026 12:48am

The owners of a pet crematorium involved in the controversial dumping of pet remains in San Jose Del Monte (SJDM), Bulacan have surfaced, admitting that they enlisted the help of bystanders or “tambays” to bury the dead pets — only to find out that the animal cadavers were thrown out at several dumping sites.

In a "24 Oras" report from John Consulta on Thursday, the owners of the Bulacan pet crematorium tagged in the dumping have surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and explained what happened.
Aliases “Michael” and “Edna”, who own a pet crematorium in SJDM, said that they were working with the Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium in Bacoor, Cavite.
Even before Ahjay could purchase the necessary equipment to cremate animals, they already began operations and accepted clients. They began passing the animal remains to the SJDM pet crematorium.

“Nung una po parang isang sako lang po talaga siya, tapos parang nasa anim o pito kapag maliliit po, tapos kapag malaki po… parang isa o dalawang aso na malaki yung dinadala, pero kalaunan po, umabot po sa isang araw ang dinala niya, parang isang dating samin, walong sako kaagad,” Edna said.

(At first it started with just one sack, then it had six or seven if they were small, then if it was big, it was one or two dogs that they were bringing, then eventually, there was one day that eight sacks were brought to us.)
The SJDM pet crematorium came to a point where they could no longer cremate all of the pet remains being brought to them by Ahjay, so they could no longer send back the ashes.
“Ang sabi niya na lang po sa akin, ‘O sige ganito na lang. Magtulungan na lang tayo. Tanggapin mo lang nang tanggapin ang lahat ng ibibigay ko, ako na bahala sa abo’,” Edna said.
(He said to me ‘O, like this. Let us help each other. Just keep accepting what I send you and I can manage the ashes’.)
Edna said she did not know where the Ahjay owner would get the ashes.
Because of how many pet remains were being brought to them, the SJDM pet crematorium owners decided to just bury the cadavers.

“Kinausap ko yung mga tambay doon sa amin, na hanap sila ng paglilibingan, maibaon nila nang maayos… ‘di ko naman alam kung anong ginagawa pagkatapos noon. Na yung iba pala, tinatapon nila. Hanggang sa dumating sa point na, tinapon na lang basta sa kalsada ng kasama niya,” Michael said.

(I spoke to the bystanders near us to look for a place to bury them, properly… I did not know what they were doing after. That some of them were just being thrown around. It reached the point that they were being thrown carelessly onto the street with his colleague.)
The couple apologized to the affected fur parents and asked for their forgiveness, saying that they wanted to take accountability for what they had done.

“Hindi po namin sinasadya. Napasubo lang talaga kami at ang huling-huling hope po namin, is mailibing siya nang maayos. Yun nga lang po, yung mga pinagkatiwalaan namin, na maglilibing po sa kanila, hindi po namin alam na tinapon lang po pala na ganun-ganun na lang,” Edna said.

(We did not mean to do it. We just bit off more than we could chew and our last hope was to bury them properly. It was just that we trusted them to bury them properly, not just throw them carelessly.)
The NBI is already attempting to get an Immigration Lookout Bulletin Order for the owners of Ajhay. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Germany’s Gen Z protests spark debate on integration, bias
articles.summary: Political debate about the recent Gen Z riots have raised the question: Can Germany talk about problems with integration without putting entire groups of people under suspicion?

image.caption: A weapon store was one target of looters and plunderers in the Frankfurt riotsImage: Kai Pfaffenbach/REUTERS

blocks.text: Responses to the violent scenes that followed recent Gen Z demonstrations in Germany have revealed differences in opinion within the federal government over who or what is responsible.

Though there is general agreement that people who committed acts of violence must be held responsible, some conservative lawmakers have largely blamed migrant groups — raising questions about whether they are identifying problems or reinforcing prejudice.

Leading Social Democrats have warned against generalizations and one CDU minister would prefer to examine the causes of the violence. Meanwhile, Gen Z's fears for the future are at threat of being overshadowed.

blocks.caption: Police officers on duty included people from ethnic minoritiesImage: Andreas Arnold/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: In Frankfurt, more than 100 police officers were injured, one severely, in the street battles that erupted after the protest on Saturday (October 31). Shops were damaged and looted, too. The situation in Cologne, Hamburg and Berlin also escalated.

Earlier, tens of thousands of young people had taken to the streets across Germany in predominantly peaceful rallies. The initiative Gen Z regelt — which roughly means Gen Z takes charge — had urged young people to highlight their fears for the future and to call for better educational opportunities, affordable housing and more climate action.
CDU initially set tone of debate

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt and Roman Poseck, Interior Minister of Hesse, the state in which Frankfurt is located, quickly set the tone of the response. Most of those arrested were German citizens, said Poseck (CDU), but added: "This group of offenders was predominantly from a migrant background."

Dobrindt, who is from Bavaria's CSU, the sister party to Friedrich Merz's CDU, said: "There were peaceful demonstrations, which into the evening were hijacked by violent left-wing groups and migrant hooligans."

Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) backed the statements made by his Interior Minister. His assessment of the background of the offenders was based on "the observations of the investigating authorities and the emergency personnel on the ground," his spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said. It also matched "the images that many have seen."

blocks.caption: The Gen Z protests across Germany were predominantly peaceful and more are planned for November 20Image: Pia Bayer/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Merz announced a tough approach toward the rioters. "Violence does not belong on our streets, and my government will show no tolerance here," Merz said, according to the script for a speech he was due to give at a closed-door CDU party event in Berlin on Monday (November 2). "Whoever attacks police and emergency services officers and loots shops attacks our freedom, ridicules society and the legitimate interests of young people."
Warnings against generalizations, focus on causes

The center-left Social Democrats (SPD), who are in a coalition government with the conservative CDU and CSU bloc, are in agreement on the point that criminals were involved. "It is criminals who attack and injure police officers and commit serious property damage," Defense Minister Boris Pistorius (SPD) told German public broadcaster ZDF on Sunday (November 1).

This is, however, where the similarities end. "What then are ‘migrant groups'?" said Pistorius, challenging the Interior Minister's choice of words. "Does that include people in the third generation living in Germany and who are German citizens? When do we stop drawing this distinction?" he countered. "I think that leads in the wrong direction."

The German federal government's integration commissioner, SPD politician Natalie Pawlik, followed up on Monday (November 2). "Always attributing such violent riots to migrant milieus is too simplistic," Pawlik told the German newspaper, the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung. "Because blanket generalizations about groups also affect those with migrant backgrounds who demonstrated peacefully or who were themselves on duty with the police or emergency services."

She said nothing justified the outbreak of violence and that such crimes had to be punished. However, Pawlik added that if investigations showed that certain groups, in particular, were involved, then the root causes also had to be named. "We cannot ignore difficult questions about the lack of prospects, experiences of marginalization or possible integration problems," the integration commissioner said.
Germany: Inclusive housing for migrants and non-migrants

German Family and Education Minister Karin Prien (CDU) also wants to examine the causes of the violent behavior. She told German public radio broadcaster Deutschlandfunk that stirring resentment "would also be politically wrong." It is much more about reflecting upon reality. "If the (perpetrators) come from migrant backgrounds then that should cause us concern," Prien said.

According to Germany's Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), some 31% of the German population have a migration background. The proportion is higher in many big cities. The figure is over 50% in Frankfurt. Prien says it is necessary to examine why integration has been less successful in some groups of immigrants than others. The real challenge lies in facilitating societal participation and preventing parallel societies.
Risk of ban on Gen Z protests?

The political discussion was intensified by the Hesse interior minister suggesting a ban on further Gen Z protests. In respect of demonstrations planned for November 20, Poseck said that the right of assembly was very valuable, but social peace just as crucial. He said there had also been "massive attacks" against the police even during the demonstrations. "The organizers do not have these gatherings under control," he added.

The organizers of the demonstrations reject those accusations. They immediately distanced themselves from the violence. Germany's Family Affairs Ministry has announced that Karin Prien is due to meet with representatives from the Federal School Students Council (BSK) as well as the German Education Union (GEW) this week.

Prien herself called for younger people's interests to be taken into account more. "These are exactly the debates we need to be having, which young people are also very rightfully demanding," she told German public regional broadcaster RBB.
This article was originally written in German

articles.title: Paraguay: President Pena resigns amid bank crisis
articles.summary: Paraguay's President Santiago Pena has resigned amid a crisis over his ties to collapsed lender Ueno. Millions of customers' accounts are frozen, with public pension and health care funds also tied…

image.caption: Pena resigned amid a banking crisis that froze millions of customers' accounts and sparked protests (FILE: 03/03/2025)Image: Bernd von Jutrczenka/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Paraguayan President Santiago Pena resigned Thursday under mounting pressure over the collapse of digital lender Ueno, as lawmakers debated his removal from office.
The bank's accounts, also used to process pension payments, are frozen, leaving millions of customers unable to access their money. Ueno also held hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds.
Why did Pena face impeachment?
Pena's resignation followed the withdrawal of support by Congress President Basilio Nunez and ruling conservative Colorado Party leader Horacio Cartes.

Thirty-five opposition lawmakers and ruling-party dissidents had submitted impeachment articles in the 80-seat Chamber of Deputies, accusing Pena of conflicts of interest, misuse of pension funds and institutional cover-ups linked to Ueno.
Pena sold his shares in Ueno Holding, whose businesses include the bank, in April 2025. Lawmakers also cited two loans he received from Ueno as part of allegations of improper financial gain.

They alleged improper presidential interference in the Social Security Institute, known as IPS, and preferential treatment for Ueno. IPS manages pension and health care funds for most Paraguayan workers and held $355 million at the bank — about 9% of its investments, according to financial manager Gladys Vera.

The motion also questioned Pena's 2023 appointment of central bank chief Carlos Carvallo, who previously chaired Financiera Ueno. According to the document, the central bank approved the company's conversion into a bank just 83 days after his appointment.
What happened to Ueno Bank?
Ueno served about 2.94 million customers, roughly 60% of Paraguay's adult population.

As of last month, the bank said it held roughly $800 million in public-sector deposits — about a quarter of its total deposits — including money from the operators of Paraguay's giant hydroelectric dams.

blocks.caption: People took the the streets of Asuncion on WednesdayImage: Jorge Saenz/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Paraguay's central bank ordered a resolution or closure process Tuesday after finding that Ueno's solvency ratio had fallen below half the required minimum.
Ueno's app, card payments and transfers stopped working, while branches closed, leaving customers queuing outside unable to withdraw their savings.
Hundreds of employees of Ueno and other companies in its parent conglomerate protested outside the Labor Ministry Thursday, demanding unpaid wages and severance.
Retirees, depositors, students and workers had marched through Asuncion a day earlier, demanding Pena's impeachment and holding signs saying "Give us back our money."
What have authorities done?

Authorities detained eight senior executives, including founder Miguel Vazquez and bank president Juan Manuel Gustale. Prosecutors also charged 27 bank officials and business associates with offenses including breach of trust and attempted fraud.
Lawyers for several detainees said they needed time to review the allegations before commenting.
Pena had sought to reassure customers in a video message Wednesday, pledging legislation "that will return to every saver what they are entitled to as quickly as possible."
The crisis also forced him to cancel his attendance at the Ibero-American summit in Madrid.
Pena, a conservative economist, took office in August 2023 for a five-year term.

articles.title: EU presses UK to guarantee discounted university tuition fees for European students
articles.summary: Failure to agree lower fees for EU citizens studying in UK should delay prized food and drink deal, members say

blocks.text: The EU is seeking a firmer pledge from the British government to guarantee European students discounted rates on university tuition fees before a much-anticipated summit this month.

At a meeting of senior EU diplomats on Wednesday, at least six member states opposed delaying a deal on tuition fees until after the summit. Many believe a failure to reach an agreement should delay the highly prized food and drink deal to cut Brexit red tape coming into force.

Andy Burnham will meet the EU leaders Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa on 20 November in Brussels, with the aim of signing three agreements – on food and drink, carbon markets and youth exchange – as well as pledging a “trusted partnership” on steel and defence industries.

But a longstanding dispute over whether EU students should pay costly international tuition fees at British universities remains unresolved and could delay the implementation of the food and energy deals, which are worth billions to the British economy.

blocks.caption: Ursula von der Leyen and Andy Burnham at the United Nations general assembly in New York City in September. Photograph: Toby Melville/Pool Reuters/AP

blocks.text: The EU wants a return to the pre-Brexit status quo where European students paid the UK domestic rate of university tuition, rather than international fees, which can be about four to six times higher for an undergraduate degree.

European Commission negotiators have proposed postponing an agreement on tuition fees by six months to ensure the success of the November event, where Burnham is expected to show his commitment to much closer ties with the EU.

But at least six member states, including in central and eastern Europe, want the university fees issue settled by the summit, while many are seeking a firmer commitment on the issue from the British government, according to four EU sources.

One EU diplomat told the Guardian: “Having a youth experience scheme without an agreement on tuition fees has very little added value,” noting the much lower cost of university education in many EU countries and therefore potential greater advantage to British students.
A second EU diplomat said there was cautious optimism about the November summit, but “a large majority” wanted “a more convincing British commitment” on tuition fees.
The British government has been contacted for comment.

For the EU, the creation of a youth experience scheme, known as Yes, which will enable those aged 18 to 30 to live, work and study on both sides of the Channel is a high priority. The erosion of people-to-people links is seen as one of the big losses of Brexit, and many European officials studied in the UK, making the issue especially resonant.

EU officials argue the bloc has leverage, saying the food and drink deal – a Labour manifesto pledge estimated to be worth £5.1bn a year to the British economy – would come into force only if there was a satisfactory agreement on tuition fees.

Similarly, the agreement to relink emissions trading systems sundered by Brexit, which would protect British exporters from European carbon taxes, could also be delayed pending agreement on tuition fees.
after newsletter promotion
A leaked version of the summit statement hints at the link between the trio of agreements, looking forward to “their joint and timely entry into force”.

Separately, EU sources have suggested without a deal on tuition fees, the EU could delay talks on British reintegration into the European electricity market that are expected to intensify next year. To secure its return to the market, the UK would have to pledge an “appropriate” contribution to European cohesion funds aimed at boosting economic development in poorer regions.

This week the Guardian reported that the UK was prepared to spend up to £450m a year to give EU students discounted university tuition fees if Brussels allowed Britain access to the Made in Europe industrial programme.
The EU said there would be no deal on Made in Europe at the November summit because the bloc was still finalising its position on the key draft law, the Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA).
Targeted at strategic industrial sectors, such as electric cars and renewables, the law would mean public subsidies and contracts would only go towards products made in Europe.

France, supported by many lawmakers in the European parliament, is pushing for a narrow definition of Made in Europe, while Germany leads a larger group of countries that don’t want to exclude trade partners including the UK.

While Britain is keen to resolve the issue, EU lawmakers are not expected to finalise the IAA text until next spring. In a significant milestone, France and Germany struck a compromise on Made in Europe favourable to the UK, but it only applies to cars, not the other industrial sectors in the IAA such as renewables and nuclear technology, or other draft proposals aimed at promoting European preference.

In a win for the UK, the draft summit statement proposes a “trusted partnership” on strategic industries, starting with steel and defence. The aim is to stop either side becoming collateral damage of the other’s trade defence measures targeted at China’s heavily subsidised imports.

articles.title: Romualdez has personal staff in jail – warden
articles.summary: Former House speaker Martin Romualdez has a personal staff staying with him around the clock in his cell at the New Quezon City Jail to “help with his daily needs,” the jail warden…

blocks.text: November 6, 2026 | 12:00am
Photo released yesterday by the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology shows former House speaker Martin Romualdez being guarded at the Quezon City Jail.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — Former House speaker Martin Romualdez has a personal staff staying with him around the clock in his cell at the New Quezon City Jail to “help with his daily needs,” the jail warden testified before the Sandiganbayan yesterday.

Supt. Maria Lourdes Pacion told the anti-graft court’s Third Division that she allowed the arrangement as Romualdez needs 24/7 assistance considering that based on her assessment, “his mental state is not yet that stable.”

“We allow that for human consideration, if the PDL (person deprived of liberty) is not in good condition because we can’t attend to all their personal needs. We cannot hire any more personnel to assign for the personal needs of Congressman Romualdez,” Pacion said.
She explained that this is not a rare arrangement within detention facilities as it is the prerogative of the jail warden to assess the needs of the PDLs.
Pacion, however, said consideration is on a case-to-case basis.

The hearing was held to determine the status of Romualdez’s detention following allegations that he was being allowed to leave the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology facility at will aboard an ambulance.

Veteran journalist Ramon Tulfo claimed that the former speaker uses a backdoor staircase at the facility to leave the premises whenever he chooses. But he has retracted the claim, saying he was “fed the wrong information.”
Pacion denied the allegations, saying Romualdez has never left the facility since his commitment there on Sept. 15.

“He stays in his cell. Once in a while he goes to the sunning area. For hearings, he goes to the courtroom in the facility. He did not go out riding an ambulance or any other vehicle,” she said. Since his detention, Romualdez has attended court proceedings remotely through video conferencing.
Romualdez’s legal team also put on record that Tulfo’s allegation was untruthful and detrimental to their client.
“That was very damaging to our client because it has a tendency to inflame the public,” they said.

The court ordered the BJMP to review closed-circuit television footage covering the period from Romualdez’s commitment to the detention facility up to Nov. 4 and submit a notarized report detailing his whereabouts based on the recordings.
It must also submit CCTV system status reports and other documentation of Romualdez’s whereabouts and his health status.
The BJMP was directed to appear before the court on Nov. 9. – Delon Porcalla, Mark Ernest Villeza

articles.title: Marcos Jr. picks Zalameda as next chief justice
articles.summary: An appointee of former president Rodrigo Duterte to the Supreme Court who has been in the legal profession for more than three decades is the country’s next chief justice.

blocks.text: November 6, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — An appointee of former president Rodrigo Duterte to the Supreme Court who has been in the legal profession for more than three decades is the country’s next chief justice.
Supreme Court (SC) Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda will succeed Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, who retires today after leading the high court for more than five years.

Presidential Communications Secretary Lino Cayetano said Zalameda’s experience across the different levels of the judicial system gives him a “comprehensive understanding of the courts and the people they serve.”

“In selecting Justice Zalameda, the President recognizes the importance of experienced and principled leadership in preserving public confidence in our judicial institutions,” Cayetano said at a press briefing yesterday.

Days before the announcement, there were speculations that Zalameda would bag the position as he was the magistrate who penned the SC First Division ruling that reversed the conviction on seven counts of graft of President Marcos’ mother Imelda.
Lawyer Ruben Carranza, a former commissioner of the Presidential Commission on Good Government, warned that the selection of Zalameda could undermine confidence in the country’s justice system.

Asked about such concerns, Cayetano replied: “Justice Zalameda served... during the time of multiple presidents... We believe in his impartiality and we look forward to working with the new chief justice.”
Before joining the SC, Zalameda led the 17th division of the Court of Appeals. He was CA justice for 11 years.

“Justice Zalameda brings more than three decades of distinguished service to our justice system. From his early years as a court official and public prosecutor to his service in the Court of Appeals and ultimately the Supreme Court, he has devoted his professional life to the administration of justice,” he added.
Cayetano said President Marcos is confident that Zalameda would discharge the responsibilities of chief justice “with integrity, impartiality, and an unwavering commitment to the rule of law.”
Zalameda was appointed to the Supreme Court by Duterte in 2019 after going through the first-ever written examinations for magistrate applicants.
Upon his appointment to the SC, he drew criticism for posing with Duterte while flashing the then president’s trademark fist gesture.

The National Capital Region Chief Prosecutors Association Inc. recently endorsed him to be the next chief magistrate, citing his leadership qualities, extensive legal experience and “unyielding pursuit of justice.”

The next chief justice obtained his law degree from the Ateneo de Manila University in 1987 under an academic scholarship grant. He joined the judiciary as branch clerk of the Makati City Regional Trial Court after passing the Bar exams in 1988. Zalameda engaged in private law practice from 1990 to 1995 then returned to government service as a public prosecutor until his appointment as the city prosecutor of Mandaluyong in 2002.

“He served during the time of multiple presidents, from the time of FVR (Fidel V. Ramos) to the time of Gloria Macapagal Arroyo to… former president Benigno Aquino III. He was eventually appointed to the Supreme Court by former president Duterte... This wide, broad experience makes him extremely qualified for the job,” Cayetano said.

Zalameda was among the five nominees endorsed by the Judicial and Bar Council for the top judicial post. The other nominees were Associate Justices Marvic Leonen, Alfredo Benjamin Caguioa, Japar Dimaampao and Jose Midas Marquez.
Servant of the judiciary

In his opening statement during his interview by the JBC on Oct. 26., Zalameda said: “I envision a judiciary that the Filipino people trust because the public believes in our integrity and accountability and because we deliver timely justice and better public service through evidence-based and sustainable reforms.”

“As a leader, the Chief Justice must first be a servant of the judiciary – attentive to litigants, lawyers, court employees, judges, and fellow Justices,” he told the JBC. “The role is to create an environment where problems are heard, solutions are developed, good ideas are supported, and people are given the tools to fulfill their responsibilities. Leadership is ultimately about service, accountability, and enabling others to succeed,” he added.
Gesmundo’s parting message
In his parting message meanwhile, Gesmundo declared his wish to leave a judiciary “ready to face future challenges with courage, competence, and compassion.”

After his appointment in 2021, he introduced sweeping changes in rules and systems in the country’s judicial and court systems through the Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovations 2022-2027, which he called “the SC’s blueprint for institutional reforms and modernization, anchored on an overarching goal of providing accessible, responsive, and real-time justice.” - Ghio Ong

articles.title: Thomas Markle’s son named person of interest
articles.summary: Thomas Markle’s son has been placed under investigation as a person of interest in a suspected child sexual abuse materials case involving electronic devices surrendered to authorities in Cebu,…

blocks.text: November 6, 2026 | 12:00am
In this screenshot, Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Duchess of Sussex Meghan, speaks in an interview with Australian morning show Sunrise in September 2021.
Sunrise on YouTube; Philstar.com screenshot

MANILA, Philippines — Thomas Markle’s son has been placed under investigation as a person of interest in a suspected child sexual abuse materials case involving electronic devices surrendered to authorities in Cebu, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said yesterday.
Remulla said investigators were looking into allegations that underage girls had been brought to Markle’s residence in Cebu, based on statements from witnesses.
“There are indications pointing to the son’s possible involvement, but he is still a person of interest and has not been treated as a suspect,” Remulla told reporters at Camp Crame.

Markle Jr. was the one who turned over the devices to authorities, but Remulla said this prompted investigators to examine his possible links to the case, including the alleged visits by minors to his house.
“He said they were just making TikTok videos, but we checked his TikTok account and did not find underage girls appearing in the videos,” Remulla said.

The investigation began after electronic devices and other personal belongings were turned over to the Regional Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking in Central Visayas on Oct. 23. The items were subsequently referred to the Philippine National Police Women and Children Protection Center for examination.
Remulla said investigators recovered about 7,500 photographs and one video involving underage boys and girls. He said some of the children depicted appeared to be as young as 10 or 11.
Initial forensic examination by the PNP confirmed the presence of suspected child sexual abuse and exploitation materials in three SD cards and one of five cellular phones examined.
Authorities stressed that the findings have yet to establish who owned, produced or distributed the materials.

The PNP secured a court-authorized warrant to examine the devices on Oct. 29. It is coordinating with the Federal Bureau of Investigation to establish the ownership of the phones, including through SIM registration records.
Investigators were also determining whether the materials belonged to Thomas Markle Sr. and whether other people were involved

articles.title: NBI to file raps vs Cavite pet crematorium
articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation will file six cases before the Department of Justice (DOJ) against a pet crematorium in Bacoor, Cavite, after finding evidence that the business allegedly buried…

blocks.text: November 6, 2026 | 12:00am
The Bacoor-based Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium is being investigated following the discovery of animal remains in Bulacan and complaints from pet owners who paid for cremation services.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) will file six cases before the Department of Justice (DOJ) against a pet crematorium in Bacoor, Cavite, after finding evidence that the business allegedly buried animals entrusted to it for cremation.

NBI Director Melvin Matibag said yesterday that the six cases involve pet owners who have come forward to file complaints, out of 25 identified customers whose animals were reportedly dumped in San Jose del Monte, Bulacan.
“We already have sufficient evidence to file the cases before the prosecution, and the evidence is strong,” Matibag said during a press briefing.

He said investigators established that Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium had been sending animals to a crematorium in San Jose del Monte because it did not have the equipment to carry out the cremations in Bacoor.

The couple operating the Bulacan facility voluntarily gave sworn statements to the NBI, with the assistance of their lawyer. They reportedly said they buried the animals because the promised cremation equipment had not been delivered.
Investigators have identified three dumping sites in San Jose del Monte, Matibag said, adding that the ashes supposedly returned to pet owners were not actually produced through cremation.

The NBI is also looking into the possible liability of other people and how the Bacoor business was able to secure permits and operate for more than a year despite its alleged lack of cremation facilities.
Matibag said the bureau was preparing to seek the issuance of an immigration lookout bulletin order against a primary person involved to prevent that person from leaving the country.
He urged other affected pet owners to come forward, assuring them that the NBI would provide assistance if they feared intimidation.
Aside from possible estafa, investigators are looking into violations of the Consumer Act and health and sanitation laws, Matibag said.
Accreditation needed

In San Fernando, Pampanga 1st district Rep. Carmelo Lazatin Jr. wants all pet crematoriums operating or intending to operate in municipalities and cities to secure accreditation from the Department of Agriculture – Bureau of Animal Industry (DA-BAI), through House Bill No. 11784 filed Wednesday.

To be known as the “Pet Crematorium Accreditation Act,” HB 11784 states that no city or municipality shall issue or renew the business permit of a pet crematorium unless the applicant presents proof of valid DA-BAI accreditation, along with all other permits, clearances, registration, and authorizations required under applicable national and local laws.

“Pets are not just domesticated animals. They become part of the family and beloved by their owners, and it is just right that they are accorded proper burial or cremation services when they pass away,” Lazatin said.
– Ric Sapnu

articles.title: Up to P30,000 incentive for government workers in December
articles.summary: Qualified government employees may receive up to P30,000 in a one-time incentive this December, subject to their agencies meeting performance and cost-saving requirements, according to new guidelines…

blocks.text: November 6, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Qualified government employees may receive up to P30,000 in a one-time incentive this December, subject to their agencies meeting performance and cost-saving requirements, according to new guidelines issued by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM).

Under a budget circular, the Collective Negotiation Agreement (CNA) incentive rewards government workers whose agencies achieved targets while reducing operating costs through jointly implemented efficiency measures.
The benefit will be paid from Dec. 15 to 31 and is not automatic. Agencies must have a valid CNA, registered with the Civil Service Commission, that provides for cost-cutting and the incentive.

The circular covers civilian personnel holding regular, contractual or casual positions, whether full-time or part-time, in national government agencies, state universities and colleges, government-owned or controlled corporations, local water districts and local government units.

Both rank-and-file and managerial employees may qualify. Non-members of the recognized employee organization can also receive the incentive if they accept the agreement’s benefits and pay the required agency fees.
DBM said the incentive may be distributed equally among eligible employees or vary according to their contribution to productivity and performance, with length of service also considered.

Workers with at least 10 months of service as of Oct. 31 qualify for the full agency-approved rate, while those with shorter service may receive prorated amounts. The maximum remains P30,000 per employee.

For national agencies and most state corporations, at least 75 percent of performance targets must have been accomplished as of Sept. 30. Local governments must similarly meet 75 percent of program targets and obligate at least 75 percent of their 2026 development fund appropriations.
Local water districts must report a positive average net income for the first nine months.
The incentive must come from allowable savings under maintenance and other operating expenses, including travel, training, supplies and utilities, rather than additional budget allocations.

For covered national agencies, the rules also require compliance with applicable cost-reduction measures, including the 20-percent savings threshold, before using available operating balances to pay the benefit.
The DBM also prohibits paying it immediately upon signing the CNA, a practice considered an unauthorized signing bonus.

Agency heads must approve the payment and submit consolidated reports by Jan. 31, 2027. Unauthorized or excessive payments may expose responsible officials to administrative, civil or criminal liability, while employees may be required to return the amounts.

articles.title: VP defense seeks subpoena for 24 witnesses
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court has been asked by the defense camp to subpoena 24 witnesses for the resumption of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial on Nov. 9.

blocks.text: November 6, 2026 | 12:00am
Impeachment court spokesperson Reginald Tongol yesterday announced the names of the witnesses who will testify during whole-day hearings from Nov. 9 to 13.
Senate SMU / Joseph Vidal
MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court has been asked by the defense camp to subpoena 24 witnesses for the resumption of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial on Nov. 9.

They are Suzette Balucanag-Punay, corporate counsel of GenCorp Industries Inc. and Metro City Chow Foods Corp.; engineer Jaime Adalin, Davao City assessor; engineer John Kenneth Enumerables, Island Garden City of Samal assessor; Vingelin Bajan, Davao City accountant; Cindy Colina, barangay chair of Matina Crossing, Davao City; Olivia Barcarse and lawyer Alvin Go of BDO Unibank; lawyers Paul Roderick Ysmael and Cesar Bernard Coloma of the Bank of the Philippine Islands; lawyer Marino Buban Jr. of EastWest Bank; Joselito Vallada of Landbank of the Philippines;

Lawyers Janella Marie Panlilio of Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co.; Jose Manuel Jr., Rodel Mediavillo and May Ann Candaroma-Morales of Philippine Savings Bank; Joseph Anthony Lopez of Security Bank; Joselito Banaag, Louiemel Panes, Rogelio Villos Jr., Jayah Deneserie Scalf and Gemma Lynn Del Mundo of UnionBank of the Philippines; as well as Anel Martin Antero from San Jose del Monte, Bulacan; Chadrin Parian from Las Piñas; and Vimar Barcellano, Quezon City prosecutor.

Political and constitutional law professor Ralph Sarmiento, said he is grateful to the defense team “for recognizing the value of the legal and constitutional views that” he has been sharing on social media.
“However, I cannot stand as witness for either side. It is important to me that I keep my independence as a constitutional law professor and as a legal analyst. I want to continue to give,” he added.
Michael Poa, spokesperson for Duterte’s defense team, said, “We respect dean Sarmiento’s personal decision and appreciate his initial consideration of our invitation.”
Threshold

Tongol confirmed that the court, through the Office of the Solicitor General, has replied to the petition filed before the Supreme Court against its decision to move the voting threshold to convict the Vice President.

“The impeachment court did not amend the Constitution; it simply ensured that the verdict will be decided strictly by the Senator-Judges who actually heard the evidence, rather than allowing absent or detained Senators who never participated in the trial to cast an artificial vote of acquittal,” Tongol said. – Evelyn Macairan, Gilbert Bayoran

articles.title: Philippines embassy in Washington hopes for immigration policy changes
articles.summary: The Philippines’ top diplomat in Washington hopes for changes in the United States’ immigration policy after the Democrats won both the House and the Senate in the midterm elections.

blocks.text: November 6, 2026 | 12:00am
US Jose Manuel Romualdez.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines’ top diplomat in Washington hopes for changes in the United States’ immigration policy after the Democrats won both the House and the Senate in the midterm elections.
Ambassador Jose Manuel Romualdez said he is hopeful of a different kind of approach on immigration.

“There could be some changes because the Democrats have been pushing for a different approach especially in detention and arrest of illegal aliens in the US,” Romualdez said in an interview on Super Radyo dzBB yesterday.
The Philippine embassy in Washington advised Filipinos in the US who have concerns regarding their status to consult a qualified immigration lawyer as the authorities began reviewing visa policy.
Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump’s visit to the Philippines to participate in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit this month is expected to be short, Romualdez said.
“Peace and security for us here in the Indo-Pacific region is important which is why President has committed,” he said.
Trump last visited the Philippines on Nov. 12–14, 2017, to attend the 31st ASEAN Summit Meeting in Manila during his first presidential term.
He is also set to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China on Nov. 18-19.
Americans in Phl insurgency?

The National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-ELCAC) yesterday welcomed reports that US authorities are looking into the possible involvement of American citizens and organizations to the communist insurgency in the Philippines.
The NTF-ELCAC said the National Democratic Front disclosed inquiries by the Federal Bureau of Investigation involving the family of an American activist detained in the Philippines.

Gabe Pasion of Anakbayan allegedly claimed during a press conference in Baltimore that his family had received repeated calls, home visits and workplace inquiries from FBI personnel and the US embassy in Manila.

In January, Filipino-American Chantal Anicoche of Maryland was recovered near an armed encounter in Abra de Ilog, Occidental Mindoro. She reportedly traveled to the Philippines intending to stay in a rebel camp before her repatriation.

Pasion’s sister, Christina, who had traveled with Anicoche, remained with the communist movement before she was taken into custody in July following a raid on a suspected communist safehouse in Laguna.
The US embassy issued a security advisory in May warning American citizens against NPA recruitment and involvement in armed insurgency activities.
“The Philippine government stands ready to cooperate and share relevant intelligence with the FBI and other competent American authorities,” NTF-ELCAC spokesperson Liza Fidelis Cañada said.

articles.title: ‘Class suspensions to be based on data’
articles.summary: The Department of Education is finalizing a comprehensive Joint Memorandum Circular to establish operational guidelines for suspending and resuming classes under Executive Order No. 130, s. 2026.

blocks.text: November 6, 2026 | 12:00am
Department of Education (DepEd) Secretary Sonny Angara.
STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education is finalizing a comprehensive Joint Memorandum Circular to establish operational guidelines for suspending and resuming classes under Executive Order No. 130, s. 2026.
Education Secretary Sonny Angara said EO 130 updates suspension rules by shifting to data-backed decisions, preventing unnecessary learning loss while keeping school communities safe.
For effective implementation, the JMC would set the operational guidelines and technical thresholds governing three distinct mechanisms for class suspensions and resumptions.

“When disasters and environmental hazards strike, our decisions must be swift, clear and firmly anchored on data from scientific agencies like PAGASA (Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration) and Phivolcs (Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology),” Angara said.
“But we must also curb learning loss by ensuring they return to class the moment conditions permit,” he added.

articles.title: Marcos to maintain enabling environment for energy cause
articles.summary: President Marcos has vowed to maintain an enabling environment for energy exploration investments as he witnessed the first delivery of natural gas from newly developed drills and wells under the…

blocks.text: November 6, 2026 | 12:00am

During the ceremonial first flow of gas at the Malampaya Onshore Gas Plant in Batangas City, Marcos said the country’s energy sector is very susceptible to geopolitical tensions, supply disruptions and price fluctuations.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos has vowed to maintain an enabling environment for energy exploration investments as he witnessed the first delivery of natural gas from newly developed drills and wells under the Malampaya Phase 4 project (MP4).
The President stressed the need to explore and develop more local energy resources, especially renewable ones, noting that more than half of the Philippines’ energy supply came from abroad last year.

“Maximizing the use of Malampaya gas could contribute to more competitive power rates because we are relying less on imported energy sources that are subject to volatile international energy prices,” he said.
Marcos said the government has awarded 14 new petroleum service contracts covering oil, natural gas and native hydrogen exploration under his administration.

The energy department, he pointed out, has granted special allowances for service contractors involved in new plays, frontier areas and gas development in remote areas to lure more exploration activities in the country.
He also described Prime Infrastructure Capital Inc. chairman Enrique Razon as “one of the bravest people” he knows, saying the risk involved in such kinds of operation is “inestimable.”
The MP4 project involved drilling two deepwater wells and installing subsea infrastructure to link them to the existing Malampaya production platform.

With an investment of close to a billion dollars, the project added about 222 billion cubic feet of recoverable natural gas reserves that can generate some 31.46 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity.
The electricity is enough to power 13.11 million Filipino households for a year.
The project marked the Philippines’ first offshore drilling campaign in more than a decade.
UN lauds Philippines commitment

The United Nations welcomed the Philippine government’s submission of the updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) under the Paris Agreements that sets a 75 percent net reduction and avoidance target for greenhouse gas emissions.

The update also broadens the scope of the Philippines’ climate commitment. It includes forestry and other land use over 2025–2035 compared with projected cumulative emissions under a business-as-usual scenario.

The unconditional component, to be achieved using domestic resources and national capacities, is seven percent, compared with 2.71 percent in the 2021 NDC, which covered 2020–2030. A further 68 percentage points are conditional on international support such as climate finance, technology transfer and capacity-building.
Malampaya wells
The $893-million project to extend the life of Malampaya field offshore Palawan has reached another milestone, successfully delivering its first supply of indigenous natural gas.
The MP4 project has begun tapping gas from the Malampaya East-1 and Camago-3 wells, providing an additional source of supply at a critical time when the country is grappling with high power costs.
Greater use of Malampaya gas “could contribute to more competitive power rates because we are relying less on imported energy sources,” Marcos said.
The Malampaya consortium, led by Prime Infrastructure Capital Inc., operates the Malampaya project under Service Contract 38 with the government. –Brix Lelis

articles.title: U.S. midterms are a 'vindication' of Alberta's approach to tariffs, says Premier Smith
articles.summary: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith says sweeping Democrat wins in the U.S. midterm elections prove her province was on the right path in the cross-border trade war.

image.caption: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith speaks to the media Monday, May 25, 2026. Smith says sweeping Democrat wins in the U.S. midterm elections prove her province was on the right path in the cross-border trade war. (Jeff McIntosh/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Edmonton·New
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith says sweeping Democrat wins in the U.S. midterm elections prove her province was on the right path in the cross-border trade war.
'We always have objected to tariffs. We know it hurts us. It hurts the Americans': Smith
· The Canadian Press
· Posted: Nov 05, 2026 10:46 AM EST | Last Updated: 30 minutes ago
"It is a vindication of our approach when it comes to tariffs," Smith told the house during question period Wednesday.
"We always have objected to tariffs. We know it hurts us. It hurts the Americans."
The Democrats on Tuesday took control of both houses of Congress and flipped long-held Republican Senate seats and state-level positions.
The results are seen as a widespread rebuke of U.S. President Donald Trump and his policies, including his treatment of trading partners like Canada.
Smith said she hopes the midterm results are an opportunity to improve the relationship between Canada and the U.S.
She pointed to her government's efforts to build relationships across the aisle, including with Adam Schiff, a Democrat senator from California.
Resisting retaliation
Smith's government has stood apart from other provinces in the trade dispute. Alberta has for the most part resisted retaliatory tariffs or trade action while encouraging continued diplomacy.
Alberta only briefly halted sales of U.S. liquor in 2025, and Smith has steadfastly opposed the idea of leveraging oil and gas exports as an economic weapon in the fight.

items: What the Republican midterm defeat means for Trump, the U.S. and Canada

blocks.text: But earlier Wednesday, as a result of the ongoing trade dispute, her government announced a new policy to prioritize Albertan and Canadian companies for small government contracts.
"We're putting local businesses first, supporting Canadian suppliers and making sure more of our government spending helps create opportunities and jobs here at home," Smith said in a news release.
The new measures apply to future contracts but existing deals are also to be reviewed when they come up for renewal.
Trump shrugs off midterm blowout as blame game kicks off
Service Alberta Minister Dale Nally said it gives qualified local companies a better shot at bidding on about $350 million in government spending, or five per cent of procurement contracts.
He said 95 per cent of government contracts already land with Canadian companies.
"This is just a practical, common-sense way that we can help businesses that we know could be struggling or impacted because of the current tariffs," Nally said in an interview.
Opposition NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi told reporters that the United Conservative Party government is two years too late.
"We've been asking for this exact thing for over two years, from the day Trump was re-elected," Nenshi said.
"Imagine the wealth you could have created and the jobs you could have created in Alberta, if you had just done it two years ago when everyone else did."

items: U.S. midterms: How Trump, Vance and Canadian politicians responded the day after Democrats' massive gains

blocks.text: Nenshi said that beyond tariffs, he feels the U.S. midterm results were a sign that voters everywhere are tired of "culture war" politics — which he accused Smith of championing.
In question period, he pointed to a government bill tabled this week that would require post-secondary schools to develop neutrality policies.
"Who exactly asked the premier for this, and what difference is it going to make to a single student?" he asked.
Smith, in response, said her government was only trying to counteract NDP policies and influence. "They create a hostile environment for free speech," the premier said.
"We're undoing their culture war."

articles.title: British comedian and actor Russell Brand found guilty of rape
articles.summary: Prosecutors labeled Brand a sexual predator, he was charged in sexual assault cases spanning from 1999 to 2009.

image.caption: Brand pleaded not guilty to the charges against him.Image: Thomas Krych/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: UK comedian Russell Brand was found guilty on Thursday of one rape and three sexual assault charges. The sentences was handed by a jury in London's Southwark Crown Court.
Brand was cleared of two rapes and one count of attempted indecent assault.

Prosecutors had labeled Brand a ruthless sexual predator and brought up charges against in cases spanning from 1999 to 2009, the years where he rose in prominence from stand-up comedy in small venues to ‌becoming a television presenter and Hollywood film star.
Judge Joel Bennathan on Thursday said Brand faced a "significant" prison term, with sentencing due Monday next week.
What has Russell Brand said?
Brand was known for risqué comedy stand-up routines and he rose to prominence in the early 2000s, hosting television programs and his own BBC radio show.
He also appeared in Hollywood films including "Forgetting Sarah Marshall" and "Get Him to the Greek."
Last year, Brand pleaded not guilty to the original charges and saying he was "grateful" for the "opportunity" to defend himself ahead of the trial.
"I was a drug addict, a sex addict and an imbecile, but what I never was was a rapist," he said about the charges. "I've never engaged in non-consensual activity."
Brand said the criminal case against him had a devastating impact on his life and family.
"My entire life has been consumed by these events, these allegations, these accusations," Brand said.

He moved away from mainstream media in recent years and relocated to Florida, where he has built a large online following with videos mixing wellness, conspiracy theories and discussions of his religious devotion.

articles.title: Iran signals satisfaction, skepticism after US midterm vote
articles.summary: While the Iranian regime says the US midterms will not change Washington's policy toward Tehran, some officials and commentators see the resounding Democratic victory as blowback against the Iran war.

image.caption: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said the election will not change the US' 'hostility toward the Iranian nation'Image: Fatemeh Bahrami/Anadolu Agency/IMAGO

blocks.text: Iran's leadership has downplayed the significance of Republican setbacks in the US midterm elections, insisting that the Democratic takeover of Congress is unlikely to alter Washington's policy toward the Islamic Republic.

"If there are still those who believe that America can be persuaded to abandon its hostility toward the Iranian nation through concessions or partisan changes in the US political system, they are gravely mistaken," Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a statement after the vote.
Khamenei also warned that Tehran would respond more forcefully to any future US military action.
The elections took place after months of military confrontation between Tehran and Washington, which disrupted global energy markets and raised fears of a broader regional conflict.
What defeat in US midterm elections could mean for Trump
Tehran likely to stick to its course despite US political shift
Mohammad Sadegh Javadi Hesar, Iran-based journalist and member of the reformist party Etemad-e Melli, said the election outcome was unlikely to affect Iran's calculations.
"Iran will not change its position simply because Republicans have lost their majority," he told DW.

According to Javadi Hesar, decisions about ending the conflict will ultimately be made in Washington. Tehran, in turn, is expected to continue insisting on its previous demands for peace, such as the end of all hostilities, including in Lebanon, and the lifting of US naval blockade.
Is a vote for US Democrats a vote against the Iran war?
Others in Iran interpreted the results more positively.
Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf argued that American voters had delivered their verdict on the Iranian conflict.
"The Americans said no to war," Ghalibaf said on X, while acknowledging that rising cost of living also contributed to Donald Trump's party losing the election.
Ghalibaf also mocked US Vice President JD Vance who had acknowledged that the Iran war was the reason the Republicans lost.
"Skip the TED talk. Why not say this to your boss?" Ghalibaf wrote on X.

Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said Iran not only challenged the United States on the battlefield and in the Strait of Hormuz but had also dealt it a political setback in Washington.
US strikes Iran hours before midterm election

Several Iranian media outlets echoed that assessment. The news website Etelaat Online sarcastically suggested that the long-discussed "regime change" had ultimately taken place not in Iran, but in the United States.
Looking back to Jimmy Carter
Some commentators drew historical parallels to another period of US-Iran tension.

The state-affiliated Mehr News Agency compared Trump's political troubles to those of former US President Jimmy Carter, recalling the failed 1980 American military operation to rescue hostages held in Tehran.

At the time, the US deployed eight military helicopters to rendezvous with six transport planes in the Iranian desert before moving on Tehran to free the hostages. However, the aircraft encountered a sand storm and a deadly crash between a helicopter and a C-130 transport plane, killing eight Americans.

The agency argued that the 1980 episode demonstrated the limits of US military power in resolving disputes with Iran. Carter went on to lose the presidential election to Ronald Reagan later that year.
Iran released the hostages in January 1981, just minutes after Reagan was sworn in for his first presidential term.
No winds of change between Iran and US
Hardline media, however, dismissed the election's broader significance.

Tasnim News Agency, which is close to Iran's Revolutionary Guards, argued that there is little meaningful difference between Republicans and Democrats when it comes to Iran policy. According to the agency, both parties pursue similar goals toward the Islamic Republic despite differences in rhetoric.
Using a Persian proverb, Tasnim summed up its view bluntly: "The yellow dog is the brother of the jackal," suggesting that neither side should be expected to act differently toward Iran.
Diplomacy rather than escalation?
Veteran Iranian diplomat Hossein Alizadeh says the actual midterm fallout is difficult to predict, but notes US politics sends ripples out across the entire world.

"The USA is a superpower and a hegemonic power. Consequently, developments in that country are of significance to the entire world — from Mexico and Canada, through the European Union, to China, and, of course, the Middle East," says in an interview with DW.

Alizadeh is an expert in international relations who served in the diplomatic corps of the Islamic Republic for 22 years , before resigning in 2010 in protest of the 2009 Iranian post-election crackdown.
US military buildup: What message is it sending Iran?

The Finland-based analyst considers another large-scale military escalation by the USA to be unlikely. While the Democrats are also opponents of the Islamic Republic, "unlike the Trump administration, they opted for a diplomatic agreement with Tehran. The 2015 nuclear deal placed Iranian nuclear activities under the oversight of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)," says Alizadeh.
He points out that the Democrats and the USA's allies were not in favor or attacking Iran.
"The negative repercussions of such a war have already become clear," he told DW.
This piece was originally published in German

articles.title: EU court says CBD foods need approval for sale before they can be certified organic
articles.summary: The EU's top court says CBD foods cannot be certified organic without approval for sale. The ruling concerns a cannabis compound whose use in food requires authorization, including before organic…

image.caption: The EU's top court ruled that CBD foods need market authorization before they can be certified organic (FILE: June 2024)Image: Monika Skolimowska/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The European Union's top court ruled Thursday that foods containing cannabidiol, or CBD, cannot receive organic certification without first being authorized for sale in the bloc.
The court said an organic label could mislead shoppers into thinking CBD foods had been approved for sale.
What is CBD, and why does it need approval?
CBD is a compound found in cannabis, commonly extracted from hemp — cannabis varieties with low levels of THC. Unlike THC, CBD does not produce a high.
The compound is widely marketed in oils, capsules and gummies as a wellness ingredient, often with claims about sleep, stress or pain relief.

The European Commission classifies CBD as a "novel food" — a food not consumed to a significant degree in the EU before May 15, 1997. Such foods require a safety assessment and authorization before they can legally be marketed.
The court noted that CBD has not yet received that authorization, although it did not say that it was unsafe.
CBD is also found in medical marijuana, but the ruling concerns its use in food rather than medicines.
What does that mean for organic certification?
The court said meeting organic production standards did not remove the need for market authorization.
"Such certification contributes to the promotion of those products and conveys, in the eyes of consumers, a positive image of quality and approval," the court said.
The restriction also covers products intended for export outside the EU.
Medical cannabis: Helpful or overhyped?
The ruling concerns CBD-based or CBD-enriched foods that lack EU market authorization, rather than all cannabis-derived foods.
Some cannabis-derived foods, such as hemp seeds and ordinary hemp seed oil, can legally be sold and certified organic if they meet the relevant standards.
Why did the case reach the court?

France's organic farming regulator, INAO, told certification bodies that CBD-based products and CBD-enriched foods could not be certified organic. It also barred CBD as an ingredient in certified organic foods, while exempting hemp oil not enriched with CBD.
A hemp industry association challenged those restrictions before France's Council of State, which referred the case to the EU court.
The French court must now resolve the dispute in line with the EU court's interpretation.

articles.title: Who is drug testing Russia's athletes, now that they have returned to international competition?
articles.summary: DW has found that three-quarters of Russia's weightlifting team had no independent out-of-competition testing before this year's world championships, despite the country's doping history.

image.caption: Russian athletes are competing under their national flag and colors at the World Weightlifting Championships in Ningbo, ChinaImage: Giorgio Scala/DBM Deepbluemedia/Insidefoto/IMAGO

blocks.text: Fresh questions have emerged over Russia's return to world sport after figures reviewed by DW showed that only four of the 16 Russian weightlifters competing at this year's world championships underwent out-of-competition testing by the International Testing Agency (ITA).

Two-time European champion Anastasiia Romanova, who previously served a two-year doping ban, was among those not tested by the ITA during the first nine months of 2026, according to its quarterly anti-doping reports.
By comparison, all 13 members of the North Korean team underwent at least one ITA test during the same period. North Korea, like Russia, has a history of doping violations in weightlifting.
Men, muscles, and the pursuit of the ‘perfect body’

The ITA, which runs weightlifting's anti-doping program, told DW that it tested all 16 Russian weightlifters "ahead of their participation in the event." DW understands those tests were conducted in Ningbo, China, where the championships are being held.

In a power sport like weightlifting, performance-enhancing drugs are most beneficial during training, when athletes build strength and muscle mass in the months before competition. Some drugs, such as anabolic steroids, may be harder to detect by the time the competition comes around.
Rob Koehler, head of the athlete-led movement Global Athlete, called the lack of out-of-competition testing "absurd."

"Out-of-competition testing is the backbone of anti-doping," Koehler told DW. "Everybody knows there's going to be testing at the event. But not everybody knows when they're going to be tested 365 days a year outside the events. It's concerning that the ITA doesn't see this as a red flag."
ITA: Russians among top 10 tested nationalities

Marta Nawrocka, the ITA's spokesperson, said that Russian athletes were among the ten most-tested nationalities in weightlifting this year. She also defended the fact that only two Russian weightlifters feature in the sport's highest-priority testing pool, saying inclusion is based on performance and risk profiles.

"Russia's history of doping in weightlifting remains an important factor in the ITA's risk assessment and testing priorities," Nawrocka said, adding that "Russian weightlifters remain subject to substantial testing activity."
Koehler, though, is unconvinced.

"You simply can't treat Russia like any other country," he said. "It has to have more scrutiny. It has to have more testing. If you don't do that, you're undermining athlete confidence in the system."
The International Weightlifting Federation did not respond to a request for comment.

blocks.caption: Only 4 of the 16 weightlifters on the Russian world championship team underwent out-of-competition testing by the International Testing AgencyImage: Giorgio Scala/DBM Deepbluemedia/Insidefoto/IMAGO

blocks.text: Sochi's enduring legacy

Weightlifting was one of the sports most implicated in Russia's state-sponsored doping scandal, which came to light after the 2014 Sochi Winter Olympics. It ranked second only to athletics for the number of positive cases identified by Canadian lawyer Richard McLaren in his 2016 report commissioned by WADA, the global anti-doping watchdog.
The scandal led to dozens of Russian athletes being banned across numerous sports. RUSADA has remained suspended for most of the past decade.

As a result, its Moscow laboratory cannot analyze urine and blood samples, meaning samples collected by the agency must be sent abroad for analysis under what WADA described as a "strict chain of custody."

blocks.caption: Russia's state-sponsored doping program came to light in the aftermath of the 2014 Sochi Winter OlympicsImage: Getty Images

blocks.text: WADA said it continued to monitor RUSADA but had been unable to gain access to the country to review the agency's suspension because of the "ongoing geopolitical situation."
It added that RUSADA had "collected thousands of samples … including hundreds from weightlifters" so far this year.

"Given the history, WADA remains vigilant when it comes to Russia," James Fitzgerald, WADA's spokesperson, told DW. "We must ensure that no stone is left unturned when it comes to verifying that all the proper testing and other anti-doping activities are taking place."
Despite being suspended, RUSADA still has the power to investigate and prosecute anti-doping cases involving Russian athletes, which critics find difficult to reconcile.
"It's a compounding problem that WADA is still giving them a free pass when it can't even get into Russia to see what they're doing," said Koehler, WADA's former deputy director general.
"There's simply no oversight and no accountability. And quite frankly, I don't think there ever really has been."
RUSADA's independence under scrutiny
Critics also argue that ongoing questions over RUSADA's leadership and independence suggest that little has been fixed in the decade since the McLaren report.
Even the International Olympic Committee (IOC), whose president, Kirsty Coventry, supports the full return of Russian athletes, has acknowledged a "lack of confidence" over RUSADA's governance.

Nawrocka said the IOC had "recently entrusted" the ITA with an expanded role within Russia in the run-up to the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028, but did not explain what the role would involve or when it might begin.

In April, investigative outlet The Insider reported that Veronika Loginova, the head of the agency, was in a long-term relationship with an alleged FSB officer. The FSB, Russia's domestic security service, played a central role in covering up positive drug tests at the Sochi Games.
Loginova did not respond to questions for this article but dismissed the allegations at the time as "all this nonsense," writing in an email that she believed "sport exists separate from politics."
WADA would only confirm to DW that its investigations unit was examining the allegations against Loginova and that the inquiry was ongoing.

articles.title: A bitter end for Ronaldo - the icon who transformed Portugal
articles.summary: As Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international football, Guillem Balague looks at why and what is next for the Portugal legend.

blocks.text: Cristiano Ronaldo's old rival Leo Messi left Argentina less than a month ago with a nation applauding him.
The Portugal legend has gone another way, and it was always going to be the case.

The 41-year-old announced his international retirement after 23 years but also after a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus which was resolved with a sanction of 30 days, that had already been served, and a fine of 255 euros.

It was the punishment imposed on the Portuguese striker for leaving the team's training camp without permission. Jesus kept him on the bench for one match and said he did not plan to start him in the next, so Ronaldo went home.
His last appearance came on 24 September against Wales. He ends his international career with 146 goals in 234 games.
A message went around Portugal with a big thank you for everything, calling Ronaldo a global ambassador and an inspiration to millions. Even so, the way it ended leaves a bit of a bitter taste.

Was he going to be named in the next squad? Possibly, as Jesus said the door was open and the decision was Ronaldo's. What is clear is that he was no longer an automatic starter, and Cristiano has never handled that well.
So is this another hissy fit? Partly, yes. He reacted the way he always has when a coach questions his place. But the label hides how much he adapted over the years.
Such a pattern appears with almost every man who sat on the Portuguese bench - there were clashes, but also communion with managers and team-mates that help explain this ending.
When a young Ronaldo first joined the squad, he arrived at camp with his baseball cap on backwards, enormous sunglasses and headphones turned up so loud they could be heard from a distance.

He would not take the cap off to eat among veterans like Luis Figo and Rui Costa. Luiz Felipe Scolari saw an extraordinary player who was immature and obsessed with showing off. He reprimanded him in public, then told him privately that if he changed his attitude, he would one day captain Portugal.

The first great disappointment came early, and it came at home. At 19, Ronaldo played in the final of Euro 2004 at the Estadio da Luz in Lisbon, in front of a country that had convinced itself the trophy was already on its way.

A single headed goal by Angelos Charisteas was enough for unfancied Greece to win it by surprise. When the final whistle went, Ronaldo could not hold back the tears, and the image of the teenager crying on his own pitch travelled everywhere.
It was a painful way to learn what a final costs, and it left him with a hunger that never really went away.

Figo owned the number 7 at the time, so Ronaldo had to have 17. Figo helped him settle but had no intention of making it easy. When he left the national team in 2006, the shirt and the team became Ronaldo's.

In September 2005, before a qualifier in Russia, Scolari and Figo went to his room to tell him his father had died. Scolari offered to send him home. Ronaldo chose to play, asked his team-mates to behave as normal, and spent time in the dressing room doing ball tricks.

That was his way to cope with the expected but still hugely hurtful passing of his alcoholic dad. He later called Scolari "father". That way the national team had become the place that held him together.

Things went sour with Carlos Queiroz. After the 2010 World Cup exit against Spain, asked to explain a poor performance, Ronaldo told journalists to ask the coach. His influence in the camp had grown so large it changed routines and habits, which explains why the coach felt undermined.

The sociologist Joao Nuno Coelho offers the best lens on how Portugal sees him. In his analysis, the national team became a representation of Portuguese identity and of the country's need to be seen internationally.
In years of economic hardship and a crisis of confidence, a team that won admiration abroad was important beyond football.
Ronaldo stood at the centre of that need and created contradictory feelings. Some Portuguese questioned his individualism and his ego, and not everyone saw themselves in his personality.
Coelho explains criticising him became more difficult as time went by. The country wanted to be proud of him and sometimes felt uneasy at the same time.

The former international Jorge Andrade told me some supporters preferred figures like Figo, Eusebio, Paulo Futre or Rui Costa. Even so, Portugal was proud to have him. And with the titles, the doubts eased.
Under Fernando Santos in 2016, he changed. He accepted playing as a centre forward next to Nani - he had never taken a coach's instructions so naturally.

After the opening draw with Iceland, he told Nani in private that he trusted Santos, and the dressing room began to see a real captain. After missing a penalty against Austria, he barely slept. Santos woke up and found him already awake.
At the training camp in Marcoussis, he took a fan's megaphone and told supporters Portugal had won nothing yet. He was enjoying the leadership role.
In the final in Paris, he left the pitch in tears, injured. He had not had the best tournament, with a muscle complaint that did not let him perform at his best.
Nani took the armband. At half-time Ronaldo pulled himself together to encourage his team-mates, and before extra time, still limping, he told Eder he would score.
And Eder did.

But the old instinct never fully disappeared. During extra-time, Ronaldo stood in the technical area giving orders until the fourth official sent him back. Other coaches I consulted found it excessive.
His greatest strength, the need to influence every result, also made limits hard to accept.
When he debuted in 2003, Portugal was still searching for its first major title. Some players mark an era, and others change a national team for good. He belongs to the second group.
That night in July 2016 gave Portugal its first European Championship.

Three years later he scored a hat-trick against Switzerland to put them into the first Nations League final, which Portugal won. In 2025 he lifted a second Nations League at an age when most players have retired.
No one has scored more goals for a national side, and no one has pulled on the Portugal shirt more times.

Under his influence, Portugal stopped being a gifted team and became one that arrives at every tournament expecting to contend, while a whole generation of players came through a dressing room where he decided what the standard was.
Coelho's point holds here as well: a small country found a way to be noticed, and for two decades he was its face.
After 2016 the question around him changed. Fewer asked whether he was selfish, and more asked whether Portugal depended on him too much.
In the World Cup in 2018, he scored three against Spain, including a free-kick after 45 attempts in major tournaments, and the team still went out to Uruguay.
After a difficult 2026 World Cup, much was made of him still starting up front when in fact statistically that was his best period.
Under Roberto Martinez, with 28 goals in 37 games, 0.756 per match, improves the 0.624 with Santos.
The federation has announced a special tribute to honour his contribution, and that is necessary as the exit has not left fans room for a celebration they want to be part of.
Not only they grew up with him, he took them to places they had not yet been.

articles.title: Alex Eala edges Czech foe in thriller, nabs Hong Kong Open quarterfinal spot
articles.summary: World No. 17 Alex Eala completes a second-set comeback against steely Czech teen challenger Tereza Valentova to reach the 2026 Hong Kong Open quarterfinals

blocks.text: POWER. Filipina tennis ace Alex Eala in action at the 2026 Hong Kong Open.
HONG KONG OPEN
World No. 17 Alex Eala completes a second-set comeback against steely Czech teen challenger Tereza Valentova to reach the 2026 Hong Kong Open quarterfinals

MANILA, Philippines – Filipina tennis superstar Alex Eala brushed off the threat of an extended match in the clutch, eking out a thrilling 6-4, 7-6(7) straight-setter against Czech rival Tereza Valentova to reach the 2026 Hong Kong Open quarterfinals on Thursday, November 5.
Down 5-3 in the second set after relentless back-and-forth action, Eala ignited the comeback fire with a love game to inch within 5-4, before completing a three-game turnaround to land at a 6-5 lead.
Valentova, however, stopped the bleeding in time to force the tiebreaker, 6-6.

Just as it looked like the 21-year-old Eala had her foe dead in the water with a 5-0 blitz in the race-to-seven finale, Valentova dug herself out with a scorching 6-1 rally of her own to set up yet another nail-biting finish for the Filipina sensation.
After four match points, Eala got the final break she needed on the serve, scoring the last two points to seal the deal and deny a valiant challenge from the world No. 85 Valentova.

“It was really, really tough. I think Tereza played incredibly, and we were able to bring the match to a really high level, and I think that was reflected on the scores,” Eala said after the match. “Really happy with that win, I think I escaped by a little bit.”

With the win, Eala also solved a yearlong puzzle featuring Valentova, as the Czech star swept the Filipina in their two previous meetings: a 6-1, 6-2 demolition in the 2025 Japan Open Round of 32 and a 7-6(6), 6-1 pullaway in the 2026 Qatar Open Round of 64.
“Of course, the previous two meetings [against her] were super difficult, so I knew it was going to be a tough battle,” Eala added. “I just tried to be better than the previous time we met.”
Eala faces another quick turnaround as world No. 81 Antonia Ruzic of Croatia awaits on the other side of the quarterfinal equation on Friday, November 6, around 7:40 pm. – Rappler.com
